IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r4.claim: The source identifies the الإنسان in both cited Fajr verses as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r4.anchor: والعشرون : أمية بن خلف . [ ومنه ] قوله تعالى في الفجر : ﴿ فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن ﴾

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r2.claim: People wrongly interpret prosperity as proof of divine honor and reduced livelihood as humiliation; both are tests under God's law.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r2.anchor: is governed by the Almighty’s law of trial.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.claim: Prosperity tests gratitude and care for others rather than pride and usurpation; hardship tests contentment rather than despair, and people should examine their treatment of orphans and the poor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.anchor: with the orphans and the poor after receiving

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r1.claim: People wrongly treat worldly abundance as proof of divine esteem and hardship as proof of humiliation; both conditions are tests, not judgments of worth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r1.anchor: The consequence of this misconception is that the first category of people is overcome by conceit and vanity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r2.claim: Affluence tests gratitude, obedience, and care for others; hardship tests contentment and resolve. Strength in both forms of trial strengthens faith and yields a peaceful soul.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p310/r2.anchor: If the Almighty blesses someone with affluence

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r9.claim: The passage rebukes Quraysh for treating wealth and children as signs of divine honor and their absence as humiliation; human is generic and the error occurs among Muslims too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r9.anchor: ذكر تعالى ما كانت قريش تقوله وتستدل به على إكرام الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari links this to God's watch over sinners: God wants obedience and afterlife concern, while people seek immediate pleasure; Abu Hayyan flags the explicit Muʿtazili claim about divine will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: بم اتصل قوله: فأما الإنسان؟ قلت: بقوله

BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.claim: The natural contrasts prepare for testing through wealth or deprivation and the opposed outcomes of tyrants and the tranquil soul.
BINTSHATI:v2p135/r3.anchor: أو بالفقر والحرمان، وما يظن معهما من إكرام أو إهانة، ثم التقابل في المصير ما بين عذاب الطاغين المغرورين، ونعيم النفس المطمئنة.

BINTSHATI:v2p149/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r3.claim: The next verses admonish people tested through either abundance or deprivation; trial can come by good or evil.
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r3.anchor: والابتلاء الإمتحان، يكون بالنعمة والخير كما يكون بالحرمان والشر:

BINTSHATI:v2p149/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r4.claim: Ikram means giving and honoring the recipient, an act of generosity and favor from the giver; ihana means humiliation.
BINTSHATI:v2p149/r4.anchor: والإكرام العطاء والتشريف للمكرم، وهو من المكرم جود وفضل. والإهانة الإذلال.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.speaker: طرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.claim: Tarafa's lines voice the pre-Islamic boast that wealth, noble children, and status reflect divine favor and rank.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r1.anchor: قال طرفة : فلو شاء ربي كنت قيس بن عاصم ولو شاء ربي كنت عمرو بن مرثد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r2.claim: Quraysh, Tamim, and others asked the Prophet to expel poor believers so they might follow him; they made the same request of Abu Talib, and verse 6:52 addressed this error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p325/r2.anchor: قالوا للنبيء أطردهم عنك فلعلك إن طردتهم أن نتبعك .

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.claim: The inserted clause in 23b–24 focuses on the human response to Hell, paralleling the worldly human responses in the secondary pair 15–16.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r7.anchor: der vor V. 25.26 eingeschobene zusätzliche eschatologische Nachsatz V. 23b.24 auf den Menschen und seine Reaktion auf die Höllenstrafe fokussiert

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r1.claim: A person wrongly thinks that God's wealth is a mark of honor, but wealth and poverty are tests allotted according to wisdom and welfare.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r1.anchor: فإني لا أغني المرء لكرامته علي ولا أفقره لمهانته عندي ولكني أوسع على من أشاء وأضيق على من أشاء

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r2.claim: True honor comes through obedience, while humiliation comes through sin, not through the size of one's provision.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r2.anchor: وإنما الإكرام على الحقيقة يكون بالطاعة والإهانة تكون بالمعصية

BURSEVI:v10p330#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p330#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p330#2/r6.claim: The next statement about the human being continues the warning: although God watches and repays His servants, people focus their attention and hopes on worldly pleasures.
BURSEVI:v10p330#2/r6.anchor: وكأنه قيل إنه تعالى بصدد مراقبة أحوال عباده ومجازاتهم بأعمالهم خيرا وشرا

BURSEVI:v10p331/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331/r1.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p331/r1.claim: Al-Suhayli says the human in these verses is Utba ibn Rabi'a, reportedly the occasion for revelation, though the description applies generally.
BURSEVI:v10p331/r1.anchor: قال السهيلي رحمه الله المراد بالإنسان عتبة بن ربيعة وكان هو السبب في نزولها

BURSEVI:v10p331/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331/r2.claim: When God grants wealth, status, and ease as a test, the human boasts that God honored him and assumes he deserved it instead of recognizing a trial of gratitude.
BURSEVI:v10p331/r2.anchor: عامله معاملة من يبتليه بالغنى واليسار

BURSEVI:v10p331/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331/r3.claim: The fāʾs explain the result of each trial, and the two clauses are balanced; the order in the first implies that he says God honored him while receiving abundance.
BURSEVI:v10p331/r3.anchor: والفاء تفسيرية فإن الإكرام والتنعيم عين الابتلاء

QASHANI:89:15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:15/r1.claim: A saying divides faith into two halves, patience and gratitude; the author uses it to require either response to God’s tests.
QASHANI:89:15/r1.anchor: الإيمان نصفان، نصف صبر ونصف شكر

QASHANI:89:15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:15/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:15/r2.claim: When tested with ease and blessings, a person must thank God by using them to honor orphans, feed the poor, and do what pleases Him, not boast of deserving them, indulge, attach to wealth, or withhold from those entitled.
QASHANI:89:15/r2.anchor: فعليه أن يشكره باستعمال نعمته فيما ينبغي من إكرام اليتيم وإطعام المسكين وسائر مراضيه

QASHANI:89:15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:15/r3.claim: When tested with poverty, a person must be patient rather than despair or claim God dishonors him; deprivation may protect him from distraction and direct him toward God, while wealth may be gradual enticement.
QASHANI:89:15/r3.anchor: أو بالفقر وضيق الرزق فيجب عليه أن يصبر ولا يجزع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated him; instead, they fail to honor the orphan.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : فاما الانسان الاية ، قال : كلا اكذبتهما جميعا ما بالغني اكرمك ، ولا بالفقر اهانك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r2.claim: Mujahid says the person wrongly assumes wealth means divine honor; real honor comes through obedience and humiliation through sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في الاية قال : ظن كرامة الله في المال وهو انه في قتله وكذب انما يكرم بطاعته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r1.claim: The surah is consistently titled Surat al-Fajr; it is Meccan, though Ibn Atiyya transmits al-Dani's report that some called it Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r1.anchor: وهي مكية باتفاق سوى ما حكى ابن عطية عن أبي عمرو الداني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r2.claim: It is tenth in revelation, after al-Layl and before al-Duha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r2.anchor: وقد عدت العاشرة في عداد نزول السور . نزلت بعد سورة الليل وقبل سورة الضحى .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r3.claim: Verse counts vary: Medina and Mecca count thirty-two, including verses 15 and 16 as separate endings; Kufa and Syria count thirty, Basra twenty-nine, with different endpoints.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r3.anchor: وعدد آيها اثنتان وثلاثون عند أهل العدد بالمدينة ومكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r4.claim: The surah warns Meccan idolaters through the precedents of ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh, announces the afterlife's punishment, and strengthens the Prophet with a promise that his enemies will pass away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r4.anchor: حوت من الأغراض ضرب المثل لمشركي أهل مكة في إعراضهم عن قبول رسالة ربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r5.claim: It refutes the belief that wealth proves God's favor and poverty His contempt, condemning failure to thank God, share with the vulnerable, and resist greed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r5.anchor: وإبطال غرور المشركين من أهل مكة إذ يحسبون أن ما هم فيه من النعيم علامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r6.claim: It warns that people will regret not preparing useful deeds; wealth cannot benefit them then, while believers benefit through faith and entry into Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p311/r6.anchor: وأنهم يندمون يوم القيامة على أن لم يقدموا لأنفسهم من الأعمال ما ينتفعون به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r4.claim: The fa and ammā make the next passage derive directly from the preceding general statement, although this inferential connection is initially obscure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r4.anchor: دلت الفاء على أن الكلام الواقع بعدها متصل بما قبلها ومتفرع عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r5.claim: Earlier peoples enjoyed blessings while ignoring messengers and acting arrogantly; the pagans similarly mistook luxury for divine favor, rejected warning and resurrection, and confined reward to wealth and punishment to poverty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p323/r5.anchor: فحصروا جزاء الخير في الثروة والنعمة وقصروا جزاء السوء على الخصاصة وقتر الرزق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r1.claim: The mistaken inference rests on denying afterlife recompense and a second life, and on imagining that present conditions last forever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r1.anchor: وهي : إنكار الجزاء في الآخرة ، وإنكار الحياة الثانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r2.claim: The fa branches from the universal watch-post statement: God's governance accords with His knowledge and wisdom, whereas the disbeliever reads ease as honor and hardship as humiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r2.anchor: هذا شأن ربك الجاري على وفق علمه وحكمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r3.claim: Thinking that wealth or scarcity proves God's approval or rejection implies that divine actions lack wisdom; the Qur'an cites the same boastful inference elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r3.anchor: وهذا التوهم يستلزم ظنهم أفعال الله تعالى جارية على غير حكمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r4.claim: God teaches believers not to let imagination or desire distort subtle evidence: worldly conditions pass and vary in duration, refuting the prevalent pagan creed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r4.anchor: وذكرهم بأن الأحوال الدنيوية أعراض زائلة ومتفاوتة الطول والقصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r5.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r5.claim: Al-Nābighah praises the Christian Ghassānids as hoping for consequences and refusing to assume that good has no evil after it or that evil is permanent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r5.anchor: قال النابغة في آل غسان الذين لم يكونوا مشركين وكانوا متدينين بالنصرانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r6.claim: Kallā rejects both inferences because each rests on a false interpretation and deluded suspicion, as the following explanation of God's testing clarifies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p324/r6.anchor: مناط الردع والإبطال كلا القولين لأنهما صادران عن تأويل باطل وشبهة ضالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r1.claim: Naʿʿamahu means that God placed him in a state of blessing and comfortable living.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r1.anchor: جعله في نعمة ، أي في طيب عيش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r5.claim: The actions are attributed to God because blessing and allotment reach people through worldly causes and the combinations of events and circumstances He established.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r5.anchor: لأن الكرامة والنعمة انساقت للإنسان أو انساق له قدر الرزق بأسباب من جعل الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r6.claim: The speech is literal, expressing the person's actual belief: people boast when blessed and complain when their needs are constrained.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r7.claim: Putting rabbī before the verb strengthens the assertion, presenting it as certain and unhesitating.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r7.anchor: أي يقول ذلك جازما به غير متردد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r8.claim: The two conditional answers recur whenever blessing or restriction occurs; the imperfect verbs convey repeated, renewed speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r8.anchor: لإفادة تكرر ذلك القول وتجدده كلما حصل مضمون الشرطين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r9.claim: Kallā rebukes reading either ease or scarcity as God's intention to honor or humiliate; worldly status does not reveal one's standing with Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r9.anchor: فهو ردع عن اعتقاد ذلك فمناط الردع كلا القولين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r10.claim: Divine intent is known through revelation, prophets and law, not worldly fortune; someone apparently wretched may be especially honored by God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p330/r10.anchor: وإنما يعرف مراد الله بالطرق التي أرشد الله إليها بواسطة رسله وشرائعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r1.claim: Kallā does not deny that God truly gives blessings; it rejects the human claim that receiving them proves God's approval.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r1.anchor: أن ما ناله من النعمة علامة على رضى الله عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r2.claim: God's reasons for worldly treatment are hidden; the ignorant should seek truth through rational evidence and revelation rather than habitual assumptions or distorted proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r2.anchor: وأن أهل الجهالة بمعزل عن إدراك سرها بأقيسة وهمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r3.claim: People of learning place things correctly and draw sound inferences guided by revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r3.anchor: وأما أهل العلم فهم يضعون الأشياء مواضعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read rabbī with a fatḥa on the yāʾ in both occurrences; the other readers leave it still.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو { ربي } في الموضعين بفتح الياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r6.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r6.claim: Readers differ on the final yāʾ in akramanī and ahānanī: Nāfiʿ has it in connected reading only, Ibn Kathīr always, and the others listed omit it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r6.anchor: وقرأ نافع : { أكرمن ، وأهانن } بياء بعد النون في الوصل وبحذفها في الوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r7.claim: The transmitted readings do not conflict with the written codex, and kallā again rejects making blessing or restricted provision signs of intended honor or humiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r7.anchor: وهو مرسوم في المصحف بدون نون بعد الياءين ولا منافاة بين الرواية واسم المصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r8.claim: The rebuke targets treating prosperity as evidence of favor, not God's actual giving of blessings; He may humiliate a disbeliever in the next life, and poverty is not imposed on every disbeliever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p331/r8.anchor: فمناط الردع جعل الإنعام علامة على إرادة الله إكرام المنعم عليه

TUSTARI:89:15/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:15/r1.claim: When some believers are tested with abundance, they mistake their provision for honor; it is instead a trial that can deceive them.
TUSTARI:89:15/r1.anchor: يعني بعض المؤمنين إذا اختبره ربه بالنعمة { فيقول ربي أكرمن } [15] بما أعطاني من السعة والرزق

TUSTARI:89:15/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:15/r2.speaker: الحسن
TUSTARI:89:15/r2.claim: Hasan says a servant remains well as long as he recognizes what can corrupt his deeds.
TUSTARI:89:15/r2.anchor: وقد قال الحسن رضي الله عنه: لا يزال العبد بخير ما علم ما الذي يفسد عمله.

TUSTARI:89:15/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:15/r3.claim: Some people are made to see their current condition as attractive, while others are overcome by desire.
TUSTARI:89:15/r3.anchor: ومنهم من يزين له ما هو فيه ومنهم من تغلبه الشهوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r3.claim: Ibtalāhu means God tested him, and naʿʿamahu means He made him blessed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r3.anchor: وابتلاه معناه: اختبره، ونعمه معناه: جعله ذا نعمة،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r1.claim: One identification of “the human” is ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa together with Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra, in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r1.anchor: أحدها عتبة بن ربيعة وأبو حذيفة بن المغيرة رواه عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أبي بن خلف قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r3.claim: Muqātil identifies him as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r3.anchor: والثالث أمية بن خلف قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the figure is the unbeliever who denies resurrection: God tests him with wealth and ease, but he assumes worldly provision proves God's favor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r4.anchor: والرابع أنه الكافر الذي لا يؤمن بالبعث قال الزجاج وابتلاه بمعنى اختبره بالغنى واليسر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r5.speaker: أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r5.claim: The people of the Ḥijāz and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ in rabbī; the speaker takes wealth as proof that God preferred him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p118#2/r5.anchor: فيقول ربي أكرمني فتح ياء ربي أكرمني ربي أهانني أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو

IBNKATHIR:89:15/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:15/r1.claim: God rebukes the person who mistakes expanded provision for honor: wealth is a trial and test, not proof of divine favor.
IBNKATHIR:89:15/r1.anchor: إذا وسع الله عليه في الرزق ليختبره في ذلك ،   فيعتقد أن ذلك من الله إكرام له وليس كذلك ،   بل هو ابتلاء وامتحان .

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ retain the yāʾ of akramanī and ahānanī in continuation but drop it at pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: أكرمني وأهانني بإثبات الياء في الوصل وحذفها في الوقف

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb preserve the two yāʾs both in continuation and pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب بإثبات الياء فيهما على الحالين

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr permits either retaining or dropping the two yāʾs in both positions.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بإثباتهما وحذفهما في الحالين

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r9.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī drop both yāʾs in either position for ease and to follow the codex, while retention follows the original form.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي بحذف الياء في الحرفين في الحالين

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r10.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb use fatḥa on the yāʾs in rabbī akramanī and ahānanī; the others use sukūn.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r10.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: ربي أكرمني وربي أهانني بفتح الياء

JISHUMI:v10p7403/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r5.claim: Testing, trying, and examining are equivalent terms; divine testing brings out the good or evil already known in a servant amid competing calls of reason, law, guidance, and Satan.
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r5.anchor: والابتلاء والاختبار والامتحان نظائر، وهو من الله تعالى إظهار ما في العبد

JISHUMI:v10p7403/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r6.claim: Ikrām is giving something good for its beneficial use, synonymous with iḥsān and inʿām and opposite to humiliating.
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r6.anchor: والإكرام إعطاء الخير للانتفاع به، ونظيره: الإحسان والإنعام

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r1.claim: The transition from God’s watchfulness to human misinterpretation is explained by several views: He watches all deeds and welfare so blessings call for gratitude and hardship for patience (Abū Muslim); He charges people with what serves their welfare before they become subject to earned recompense; or their ignorance mistakes welfare for honor or humiliation.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r1.anchor: قلنا: فيه وجوه: أحدها: أنه بالمرصاد لأعمالهم، ولهم، لا يخفى عليه شيء من مصالحهم

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.claim: The rebuke “rather, you do not honor” answers the claim that restricted provision means God is humiliating people: their own neglect is the fault.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.anchor: لما رد عليهم ظنهم أن التقدير الإهانة، بين أن الإهانة لهذا، لا لما قالوا

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r3.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf, who mistook being blessed for esteem without gratitude, and restricted provision for contempt.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r3.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (فأما الإنسان) في أمية بن خلف، امتحنه الله بالنعمة

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r2.claim: People mistakenly regard prosperity as divine honor and hardship as humiliation; actual recompense is in the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r2.anchor: فيظن النعمة كرامة وجزاء، والمحنة إهانة، جهلا منه، وإنما الجزاء في يوم القيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r1.claim: The human passage connects to God's lying in wait: God seeks obedience and final success and has punishment ready for the disobedient, whereas people care only for immediate pleasures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r1.anchor: إن الله لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة والسعي للعاقبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r2.claim: The two clauses are syntactically balanced by an understood pronoun before the second condition; the first fa-yaqulu is the predicate of al-insan, with the intervening time clause delayed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r2.anchor: وأما هو إذا ما ابتلاه ربه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r3.claim: Both abundance and restriction are tests: abundance tests gratitude against denial, and restriction tests patience against despair, as the verse about testing with good and evil confirms.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r4.claim: God's withholding is not humiliation; failing to grant a favor is an absence of generosity, not an insult, just as not receiving a gift is not being insulted.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r5.claim: The first rebuke may target the claim that wealth proves deserved honor: God gives freely, with piety rather than ancestry or status as the relevant criterion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r5.anchor: لأنه قال على قصد خلاف ما صححه الله عليه وأثبته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the rebuke also targets calling a lack of new gifts humiliation, despite acknowledging God's prior favors; not receiving generosity is not being demeaned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r6.anchor: أن ينساق الإنكار والذم إلى قوله : { ربى أهانن }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p752#2/r7.claim: Qira'at include a light or doubled dāl in qaddara; at pause, the final nūn is still and the yā is omitted, with its kasra retained in connected speech.

MUQATIL:89:15-22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf and ʿAbd Allāh b. Nufayl: after Nufayl advised him to do good and avoid evil, Umayya cited 47:11, asked why God enriched him but impoverished Nufayl, then claimed wealth proved his honor; Ibn Khaṭal said God might indeed have done so.
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r1.anchor: نزلت الآية في أمية بن خلف الجمحي، وعبدالله بن نفيل، أتاه يأمره بالمعروف، وينهاه عن المنكر

MUQATIL:89:15-22/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r2.claim: Wealth does not show God's honor or poverty His contempt: God meant to give the rich man ease in this life and make the poor man's reckoning lighter in the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r2.anchor: كلا ما أغنيت هذا الغنى لكرامته، ولا أفقرت هذا الفقير لهوانه علي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r1.claim: A person wrongly treats abundance as honor and restricted provision as humiliation; God tests with wealth to see gratitude and with poverty to see patience, while the person seeks only immediate pleasure.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r1.anchor: وهو قد عكس فإنه إذا امتحنه ربه بالنعمة والسعة ليشكر قال ربى أكرمنى أى فضلنى بما أعطانى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r2.claim: The reading qaddara is attributed to the Syrian readers and Yazid and means God constricted provision until it sufficed for subsistence.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#8/r2.anchor: أى ضيق عليه وجعله بمقدار بلغته فقدر شامى ويزيد

QUTB-ZILAL:89:15/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:15/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:15/r1.claim: People mistake wealth or status for proof that God honors and has chosen them, confusing a test that precedes reward with reward itself.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:15/r1.anchor: إنما يحسب هذا الرزق وهذه المكانة دليلا على استحقاقه عند الله للإكرام

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r1.claim: The passage connects the claim about provision to God watching over people in the Hereafter: worldly people focus only on pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r1.anchor: قوله : { فأما الإنسان } متعلق بقوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد } ( الفجر : 14 ) كأنه قيل : إنه تعالى لبالمرصاد

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r2.claim: The mistake is to treat worldly comfort as proof of honor and hardship as proof of humiliation, as people heed only worldly appearances.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r2.anchor: فإن وجد الراحة في الدنيا يقول : ربي أكرمني ، وإن لم يجد هذه الراحة يقول : ربي أهانني

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r3.claim: Worldly fortunes are negligible beside the Hereafter: earthly pleasure is no honor if its owner is damned, and hardship is no disgrace if its sufferer is saved.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r3.anchor: أن سعادة الدنيا وشقاوتها في مقابلة ما في الآخرة من السعادة والشقاوة كالقطرة في البحر

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r4.claim: Neither prosperity nor pain proves desert, since God may expand provision to sinners or restrict it for righteous people for reasons including decree, wisdom, or testing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r4.anchor: وثانيها : أن حصول النعمة في الدنيا وحصول الآلام في الدنيا لا يدل على

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r5.claim: The prosperous must remember the outcome, while the poor should remember blessings such as health, reason, faith, and protection from harm.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r5.anchor: فالأمور بخواتيمها ، والفقير والمحتاج لا ينبغي أن يغفل عما لله عليه من النعم

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r6.claim: Material pleasures can distract the soul from God; being denied them can redirect a person toward worship and greater happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r6.anchor: أما إذا لم يحصل للإنسان شيء من هذه المحسوسات رجعت شاءت أم أبت إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r7.claim: Greater and more durable worldly attachment increases grief at death, while lesser attachment can lead to greater posthumous happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r7.anchor: فكل من كان وجدانه للدنيا أكثر وأدوم كانت محبته لها أشد ، فكان تألمه بمفارقتها عند الموت أشد

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r8.claim: Razi links this worldly fixation to people who know only the outward life and to worshippers who turn away when tested.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r8.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في صفة الكفار : { يعلمون ظاهرا من الحيواة الدنيا وهم عن الاخرة هم غافلون

RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r9.claim: The example of a person worshipping at the edge shows worldly benefit can make him content while a trial makes him turn away.
RAZI-FULL:v31p154#2/r9.anchor: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r1.claim: Razi says his arguments presuppose resurrection; without any afterlife, wealth and deprivation would determine happiness and misery.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r1.anchor: هذه الوجوه إنما تصح مع القول بإثبات البعث روحانيا كان أو جسمانيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r2.claim: Even without resurrection, wealth might bring murder, robbery, or suffering, while deprivation might preserve safety, so present wealth alone still proves nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r2.anchor: ربما كان وجدان الدنيا الكثيرة سببا للقتل والنهب والوقوع في أنواع العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r3.claim: One view identifies the two humans as ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra, reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r3.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس أنه عتبة بن ربيعة ، وأبو حذيفة بن المغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r4.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي : هو أبي بن خلف

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r5.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r5.claim: Muqātil says the passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r6.claim: Another reading takes “the human” as anyone characterized by denial of the Day of Recompense.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r6.anchor: أن المراد من كان موصوفا بهذا الوصف وهو الكافر الجاحد ليوم الجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r7.claim: Both expanded and restricted provision are trials: abundance tests gratitude and scarcity tests patience, as in 21:35.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r7.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد ، فإذا بسط له فقد اختبر حاله أيشكر أم يكفر

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r8.claim: The particle “no” may deny only the person's claim of being humiliated; alternatively, it may reject both claims of honor and humiliation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r8.anchor: لأن كلمة الإنكار هي قوله : { كلا } فلم لا يجوز أن يقال : إنها مختصة بقوله : { ربى أهانن

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r9.claim: If both claims are rejected, one error is assuming the wealth was deserved.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r9.anchor: أحدها : أنه اعتقد حصول الاستحقاق في ذلك الإكرام

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r10.claim: He ignores the prior gifts of health, reason, and religion, showing he is boasting rather than thanking God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r10.anchor: فلما لم يعترف بالنعمة إلا عند وجدان المال ، علمنا أنه ليس غرضه من ذلك شكر نعمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r11.claim: Boasting of worldly gifts while ignoring the Hereafter indicates denial of resurrection, like the man who doubted that his garden would perish.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155/r11.anchor: يدل على كونه منكرا للبعث ، فلا جرم استحق الذم على ما حكى الله تعالى ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r1.claim: The first clause uses fa and the second wa because mercy and blessing precede wrath and pain; fa also suits the more frequent blessings, as in 14:34.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r1.anchor: لأن رحمة الله سابقة على غضبه وابتلاءه بالنعم سابق على ابتلائه بإنزال الآلام

RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r2.claim: The wealthy person's claim of being honored is true in the limited sense that he received wealth, but calling scarcity humiliation is false.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r2.anchor: لأنه في قوله : { أكرمن } صادق وفي قوله : { أهانن } غير صادق فهو ظن قلة الدنيا وتقتيرها إهانة

RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r5.claim: At pause, some readings leave the nūn sākin after dropping the yāʾ in the connected form, its kasra sufficing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p155#2/r5.anchor: وأكرمن وأهانن بسكون النون في الوقف فيمن ترك الياء في الدرج مكتفيا منها بالكسرة

SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r1.claim: Fa-ammā al-insān is a topic whose predicate is the sentence fa-yaqūlu; the ẓarf is fronted in meaning, and the intervening fāʾ does not prevent that analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r1.anchor: أحدهما: وهو الصحيح أنه الجملة من قوله " فيقول " كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ instead makes idhā conditional, with fa-yaqūlu as its answer and the full conditional as the topic's predicate; the author objects that ammā requires fāʾ in its predicate except after omitted qawl or in necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن " إذا " شرطية وجوابها " فيقول " ، وقوله " فأكرمه " معطوف على " ابتلاه "

SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects the human's reaction to God's watchfulness and says God wants only obedience, whereas the human wants only immediate life.
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت بم اتصل قوله " فأما الإنسان "؟ قلت:

SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r4.claim: The author rejects the exclusivity claim theologically: God wills obedience and other events too, so the wording should say God wants obedience from people without saying only that.
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r4.anchor: ومذهبنا أن الله يريد الطاعة وغيرها، ولولا ذلك لم يقع.

SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r5.claim: The two ammā clauses are structurally balanced because the second has an implicit huwa; each predicate is fa-yaqūlu, with the temporal clause deferred after the topic.
SAMIN-DURR:89:15/r5.anchor: هما متوازنان من حيث إن التقدير: وأما هو إذا ما ابتلاه ربه

STUDYQURAN:89:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r1.claim: People wrongly treat wealth and status as proof of worth before God, forgetting that God expands or constricts provision and that nobility is reverence.
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r1.anchor: Human beings are inclined to think that wealth and status are marks of true worth or signs of one’s standing with God

STUDYQURAN:89:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī links these verses to heedlessness about the Hereafter and to worship on a brink, showing that worldly good may harm in the next life and apparent abasement may become honor; attachment to sensory life makes departure harder.
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī connects the present verses to 30:7

STUDYQURAN:89:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r3.speaker: God in a ḥadīth qudsī
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r3.claim: God says worldly abundance or paucity does not itself honor or abase; honor comes through obedience and abasement through disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:89:15/r3.anchor: I only honor one whom I have honored with obedience unto Me

TAB-FULL:v24p376/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p376/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p376/r1.claim: Qatāda comments that the person has reason to say this when God grants him such blessings.
TAB-FULL:v24p376/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه فأكرمه ونعمه فيقول ربي أكرمن} [الفجر: 15] وحق له

TABATABAI:89:9-15/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r9.claim: The human being is under divine watch and tested by both abundance and restricted provision, but wrongly treats wealth as proof of honor and poverty as proof of humiliation, then transgresses or despairs.
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r9.anchor: وأما الإنسان فإنه إذا أنعم الله عليه بنعمه حسب أن ذلك إكرام إلهي له أن يفعل بها ما يشاء

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r1.claim: Al-insān refers to the human type by its ordinary disposition, with the definite article marking a genus rather than every individual.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r1.anchor: المراد به النوع بحسب الطبع الأولي فاللام للجنس دون الإستغراق

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r2.claim: God’s testing encompasses both granting and withholding provision; outward honor and comfort are initially gifts meant to elicit gratitude and worship, but humans can turn them into a cause of punishment.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r2.anchor: أن إيتاء النعم والإمساك عنه جميعا من الابتلاء والامتحان الالهي

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r3.claim: The statement “my Lord honored me” reports how a person perceives the gift as lasting divine approval and permission to do as he wishes; the wording reflects innate acknowledgment of God even if the tongue resists it.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r3.anchor: مبني على اعترافه بحسب الفطرة به تعالى وإن استنكف عنه لسانا

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r5.claim: Human happiness is wrongly equated with worldly comfort and misery with deprivation; true honor is nearness to God through faith and good works, regardless of wealth or poverty, since both are tests.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r5.anchor: والحال أن الكرامة هي في التقرب إليه تعالى بالإيمان والعمل الصالح سواء في ذلك الغنى والفقر

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r6.claim: He leaves aside other interpretations of the two verses because he judges them of little benefit.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r6.anchor: ولهم في معنى الآيتين وجوه أخر تركنا التعرض لها لقلة الجدوى

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r2.claim: Ibtalā means tested; God's favor and increase in provision lead the person to say that his Lord honored him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r2.anchor: والمعنى إذا ما اختبره ربه وأوسع عليه فيقول ربي أكرمن

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r4.claim: Kallā rejects the person's equation of worldly abundance with honor and poverty with humiliation; this is the unbeliever who denies resurrection, whereas the believer sees honor in success toward the afterlife.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r4.anchor: وهذا يعنى به الكافر الذي لا يؤمن بالبعث، وإنما الكرامة عنده والهوان بكثرة الحظ في الدنيا،

THALABI:v10p200#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p200#2/r1.claim: God tests a person with wealth and ease; he celebrates this as honor, but when tested with poverty and constricted provision calls it humiliation, forgetting to thank God for health and sound limbs.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r1.anchor: فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه امتحنه ربه بالنعمة والوسعة. فأكرمه بالمال

THALABI:v10p200#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p200#2/r2.claim: Qatāda comments on how quickly the child of Adam disbelieves or denies.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: ما أسرع كفر ابن آدم

THALABI:v10p200#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p200#2/r3.claim: Most readers use the light form of qadara; Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir geminate the dāl, and both are accepted Arabic forms.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r3.anchor: وقراءة العامة فقدر بتخفيف الدال، وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر بالتشديد، وهما لغتان

THALABI:v10p200#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v10p200#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes qadara as constricting provision from qaddara as giving enough; adequate provision would not prompt the complaint that God humiliated him.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r4.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو يقول: قدر بمعنى قتر وقدر هو أن يعطيه ما يكفيه

THALABI:v10p200#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p200#2/r5.claim: ‘No’ rejects the assumption that wealth signals honor and poverty humiliation: both are God's decree; He honors through obedience and humiliates through disobedience, not worldly abundance or scarcity.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r5.anchor: ثم رد عليه فقال: كلا لم أبتله بالغنى لكرامته علي ولم ابتله بالفقر لهوانه علي

THALABI:v10p200#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p200#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the person should praise God in either abundance or poverty.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: معنى كلا لم ينبغ له أن يكون هذا ولكن ينبغي أن يحمده على الأمرين

THALABI:v10p200#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p200#2/r7.claim: The next ‘rather’ explains that deprivation follows their failure to honor the orphan.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r7.anchor: ثم قال: بل لا تكرمون اليتيم يعني أهنت من أهنت من أجل أنه لا يكرم اليتيم

THALABI:v10p200#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r8.speaker: أهل البصرة
THALABI:v10p200#2/r8.claim: The people of Baṣra read the subsequent verbs in the third person, while the other readers address the audience directly.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r8.anchor: فقرأ أهل البصرة يكرمون وما بعده كله بالياء، وقرأها الآخرون بالتاء

THALABI:v10p200#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة
THALABI:v10p200#2/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and the Kufans read taḥāḍḍūna with an extra alif and fatḥa on tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī has a rare ḍamma form, and others read taḥuḍḍūna without the alif.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r9.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة تحاضون بالألف وفتح التاء

THALABI:v10p200#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p200#2/r10.claim: Turāth means inheritance and aklan lammā means a voracious eating that gathers everything.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r10.anchor: وتأكلون التراث الميراث أكلا لما شديدا

THALABI:v10p200#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p200#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says people eat their own inheritance and that of others.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r11.anchor: قال الحسن: يأكل نصيبه ونصيب غيره

THALABI:v10p200#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r12.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v10p200#2/r12.claim: Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh calls it abuse in inheritance: consuming one's own and others' shares.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r12.anchor: بكر بن عبد الله: اللم الاعتداء في الميراث يأكل ميراثه وميراث غيره

THALABI:v10p200#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p200#2/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd says they devoured everything they found without asking whether it was lawful, including women’s and children’s inheritance, which they withheld; he cites 4:127.
THALABI:v10p200#2/r13.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا لا يورثون النساء ولا الصبيان، وقرأ يستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم

THALABI:v10p200#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p200#2/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v10p200#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains lammam with the ordinary use ‘I gathered everything on the table and ate it all.’
THALABI:v10p200#2/r14.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة يقال: لممت ما على الخوان إذا أتيت على ما عليه وأكلته كله

ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n8/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari, Razi, Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n8/r1.claim: They read the contrast introduced by fa-amma as connecting back to the evidence for truth in verse 5: people usually focus on this world's immediate gains rather than the hereafter.

ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n9/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n9/r1.claim: Razi says the person treats God's bounty as something owed to him.
ASAD-NOTES:89:15#n9/r1.anchor: he regards God's bounty as something due to him (Razi)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r1.claim: The person tested with prosperity is identified as Utba ibn Rabi‘a and Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد عتبة بن ربيعة، وأبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r2.claim: He is the unbeliever Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هو الكافر أبي بن خلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r3.claim: The passage was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في أمية بن خلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r4.claim: God tests him with wealth and ease, then provides and bestows abundance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r4.anchor:
اختبره بالغنى (¬7) واليسر (¬8).
{فأكرمه ونعمه} رزقه وأنعم عليه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r5.claim: “Honored” here means given wealth and worldly good, not honored as the opposite of humiliation; God gives worldly prosperity to unbelievers without truly honoring them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r5.anchor: الذي هو (نقيض الهوان، ولكنه من الإكرام الذي هو) (¬1) إعطاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r6.speaker: مقاتل، ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r6.claim: The person wrongly assumes that God’s gift of worldly goods means He has favored him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p508/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: فضلني بما أعطاني؛ ظن أن ما أعطاه من

WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r1.claim: “The human” means the disbeliever, whose prosperity is a trial through wealth and expanded means.
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r1.anchor: يعني الكافر { إذا ما ابتلاه ربه } امتحنه بالنعمة والسعة

WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r2.claim: He wrongly takes worldly abundance alone as proof that God honored him.
WAHIDI-QT:89:15/r2.anchor: لا يرى الكرامة من الله إلا بكثرة الحظ من الدنيا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r3.claim: The human here means the disbeliever, whose trial is prosperity and abundance; he treats wealth as proof that God honored him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r3.anchor: يعني: الكافر { إذا ما ابتلاه ربه } امتحنه بالنعمة والسعة { فأكرمه } بالمال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r4.claim: The disbeliever fails to recognize divine honor except as a large share of worldly goods.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r4.anchor: لا يرى الكرامة من الله إلا بكثرة الحظ من الدنيا

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r19.claim: The heedless person watches worldly pleasures: God’s testing assigns duties and makes a person accountable in the afterlife according to performance.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r19.anchor: mükellef kılar, ibraz edeceği hâle göre âhirette mes’ul etmek

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r20.claim: Honor means bringing someone forward with worldly status, while bestowing abundant blessings means increasing provision and wealth.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r20.anchor: hoşuna gidecek ikbal ve câh ile yüze çıkarır

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r21.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r21.claim: Ebussuud, followed by Alusi, treats the fā before “honored him” as explanatory, making honor and blessing identical with the trial.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r21.anchor: Ebussuud ve ona tebe‘an Âlûsî فَأَكْرَمَهُۥ’da “fâ”yı tefsîriye addetmiş

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r22.claim: The author rejects that analysis: the fā is causal, and the honor and blessing are specifically granted through the trial and its duties, so the two expressions differ.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r22.anchor: fikrimizce bu doğru değildir. Bu فَا sebebiye olmalıdır

ELMALILI:89:10-15/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r23.claim: The heedless person treats trial-bound worldly favor as unconditional honor, imagines himself permanently beloved, ignores accountability, and falls into pleasure-seeking, excess, corruption, and loss.
ELMALILI:89:10-15/r23.anchor: Kendisini Allah’ın ilelebed mükrem kıldığı sevgili kullarından imiş gibi farzeder

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r1.claim: The rhyme between ʾakramanī and ʾahānanī is approximate, requiring Kā to count like KKa; pairs 23–24 and 29–30 rhyme similarly loosely.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Beide Verse stehen nur in einem nährungsweisen Reimverhältnis

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r2.claim: Meccan and Medinan verse divisions split each verse in two; Neuwirth supports this because of their unusual length, but the author says that is inconclusive given their likely insertion.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zugunsten dieser Abteilung lässt sich auch mit der „unverhältnismäßigen Länge“ der beiden Verse argumentieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r3.claim: Subdivision would yield a cross-rhyme like 101:6–9, though Neuwirth's proposed rhyme in 69:19 and 69:25 relies on unusual vowel equivalence and a long six-verse gap; division is doubtful.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Insgesamt erscheint eine Abteilung innerhalb von V. 15 und V. 16 deshalb eher zweifelhaft.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.claim: The likely later-added verses use the ʾakrama–ʾahāna opposition and echo verse 17's failure to honor orphans, adding an unstable relation to God alongside social sins; other texts name its positive opposite with ṣ-b-r.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die beiden später hinzugefügten (s. o.) Verse 15.16, die terminologisch auf der Opposition

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r1.claim: Meccan polytheists defended their way by treating abundant wealth as proof of divine favor and reduced provision as humiliation; the verses expose the arrogance behind that inference.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r1.anchor: kendi yollarının doğru olduğunu, nitekim bu sayede Allah tarafından kendilerine bol nimetler ve servetler ikram edildiğini savunuyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r2.claim: The ‘human’ especially means Meccan polytheists of this character: prosperity is a test and gift, not proof of merit, and calls for gratitude and sharing rather than a bare boast that God favored them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r2.anchor: nimetlerle bir sınamadan geçirildiğini, bunların bir hikmetle kendisine verildiğini düşünerek şükrünü yerine getirmesi gerekirken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.claim: Passing life’s test requires gratitude for God’s unearned gifts and patience when they are withheld, plus sharing with the poor and vulnerable and encouraging organized social solidarity; Meccan ethics summarize this as reverence for God’s command and compassion for His creatures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.anchor: bu hususta toplumsal bir duyarlılığın gelişmesine, dayanışma ve yardımlaşmanın kurumsal bir hale gelmesine katkıda bulunmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.claim: The passage sharply criticizes polytheist arrogance, selfish indifference to others, and mad attachment to wealth while teaching Muslims the religious and moral basis for life under God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.anchor: müşrik Araplar’daki Allah’a karşı küstahlık derecesine kadar varan benlik iddiası, “öteki”ne karşı tam bir sorumsuzluk ve ilgisizliğe götüren egoizm ve çılgınca bir mal tutkusu

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr in the Yazīdī transmission retains yāʾ in akramanī and ahānanī in both pause and liaison.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r1.anchor: أكرمني [الفجر/ 15] وأهانني [الفجر/ 16] بياء في الوصل والوقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r2.claim: These readers omit yāʾ from akraman and ahānan in both liaison and pause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r2.anchor: أكرمن وأهانن بغير ياء في وصل ولا وقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r3.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r3.claim: Many Nāfiʿ transmitters, including Qālūn, Warsh, and others, retain yāʾ in liaison; one report has yāʾ from the people of Medina.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r4.claim: Reports from Abū ʿAmr vary: he permits either form in liaison but pauses at the nūn, with some transmitters matching Nāfiʿ or the readers who omit yāʾ throughout.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r4.anchor: ما أبالي كيف قرأت أبالياء أم بغير الياء في الوصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r5.claim: Abū Zayd describes akraman and ahānan as jussive nūns with the yāʾ deleted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r5.anchor: أكرمن وأهانن مجزومتا النون، محذوفتا الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r6.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr keeps yāʾ in the verb even at pause because verbs retain final yāʾ where nouns such as qāḍin and ghāzin lose it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r6.anchor: أن الفعل لا يحذف منه في الوقف، كما يحذف من الأسماء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r7.claim: Even letters normally retained may be omitted in poetic rhyme and Qurʾānic endings; Sibawayh calls such endings pauses and allows deletion in complete clauses resembling a pause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r7.anchor: وجميع ما لا يحذف في الكلام، وما يختار فيه أن لا يحذف نحو: القاضي

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r8.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r8.claim: Pause permits changes to strong consonants too, so endings that resemble added letters are also deleted, just as feminine tāʾ is commonly dropped in vocative shortening.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403#2/r8.anchor: أن الفواصل والقوافي مواضع وقف، والوقف موضع تقرير

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r1.claim: Weak endings derived from lām and other suffixes are deleted under jussive and in speech, showing that they can behave like extra letters; this supports deletion at verse endings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r1.anchor: وحذفوا اللام وسووا بينها وبين الزائد في الحذف للجزم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r2.claim: Sibawayh’s “more analogical” means closer to the retained underlying form, while deletion remains frequent Arabic and is especially apt at pauses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r2.anchor: فإنه يجوز أن يعنى بقوله: أقيس الكلامين، القياس على الأصل الذي هو متروك

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r3.claim: Yāʾ deletion occurs even outside pauses, as in Q 11:105, so it is still more fitting at verse endings such as Q 89:9.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r3.anchor: وإذا كانوا قد حذفوا في مواقع ليست بموضع وقوف، نحو قراءة من قرأ: يوم يأت

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ’s connected form retains yāʾ because there is no pause, while his paused form omits it; Abū ʿAmr is also reported with both this and another pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r4.anchor: فإذا لم يقف عليها صار بمنزلة غيرها من المواضع التي لا يوقف عليها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit yāʾ in both settings, treating the verse ending as a pause that changes the word by deletion.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p405/r5.anchor: يدل أن هذا موضع وقف، فغير بالحذف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.claim: In أكرمن and أهانن, one reading keeps yāʾ in connected speech but drops it at pause, with an unvowelled nūn; al-Aʿshā’s verse witnesses this ending.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ أكرمن ﴾ و ﴿ أهانن ﴾ يقرأ بإثبات الياء فيهما وصلا وحذفها وقفا

QIRAAT-ER:89:15:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:14#1/r1.claim: The canonical reading opens the first-person possessive yāʾ with -a, smoothing its transition into akramani.
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:14#1/r1.anchor: opens or releases the first-person possessive yāʾ with -a, smoothing the transition

QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#1/r1.claim: The reading pronounces the first-person suffix with full final yāʾ, making the word for me fuller at the verse ending.
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#1/r1.anchor: pronounces the first-person suffix with full final yāʾ, making ""me"" phonetically fuller

QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#2/r1.claim: The pause form shortens akraman and the connected form restores akramanī, making final yāʾ recitation-sensitive.
QIRAAT-ER:89:15:15#2/r1.anchor: Canonical pause/continuation variant shows a waqf-like shortened akraman followed by full akramanī

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r1.claim: The passage continues the warning: God watches for the afterlife, while people care only for worldly pleasure, becoming content when they get it and resentful when they do not.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r1.anchor: كأنه قيل أنه سبحانه لبالمرصاد من أجل الآخرة فلا يطلب عز وجل إلا السعي لها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r2.claim: An alternative makes the sentence follow as a consequence: the rich person becomes arrogant and the poor person despairs and says what should not be said; al-Alusi dismisses this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r2.anchor: وقيل هو متصل به متفرع عليه على معنى فالإنسان يؤاخذ لا محالة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r3.claim: God treats abundance as a test of gratitude; the fa in “honored him and gave him ease” explains what the test consists of, and the two actions are expressed as one in the person's reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r3.anchor: بتلاه ربه أي عامله معاملة من يبتليه بالغنى واليسار ليرى هل يشكر أم لا والفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r4.claim: The clause “my Lord honored me” is the predicate about the person; because “when” is delayed, it modifies “he says,” and the fa does not prevent this syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r4.anchor: وهذه الجملة خبر للمبتدأ الذي هو الإنسان والفاء لما في أما من معنى الشرط والظرف أعني إذا متعلق بيقول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, Abu Hayyan, al-Samin, al-Safaqisi, and many commentators allow “when” to modify “he says” despite its post-fa position; al-Shihab calls this correct.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r5.anchor: كما صرح به الزمخشري وغيره من متقدمي النحاة وتبعهم من بعدهم كأبي حيان والسمين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r6.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r6.claim: Al-Radi and those following him, including al-Damamini, allow post-fa advancement only when the advanced phrase is the sole separator after “as for”; a second separator is disallowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r6.anchor: وخالفهم في ذلك الرضي ومن تبعه كالبدر الدماميني في شرح المغنى فقالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r7.speaker: الجلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r7.claim: Al-Jalabi claims this restriction is agreed and rejects the earlier parsing, proposing instead an omitted predicate such as “as for the person's state when …”.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r7.anchor: وزعم الجلبي محشي المطول إن هذا متفق عليه فرد به على المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi objects that the proposed “state” would make “he says” its predicate only through strained interpretation, so that rescue is not sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p125#2/r8.anchor: ويرد على تقديره أنه لآ يصح وقوع جملة يقول خبرا عن الشأن إلا بتعسف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126/r1.claim: The preceding grammatical rescue avoids one difficulty only by fleeing from cloud to gutter, a proverb-like criticism; Abu al-Baqa instead makes “when” conditional and “he says” its answer, requiring an omitted clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126/r1.anchor: وهو فرار من السحاب إلى الميزاب وذهب أبو البقاء إلى أن إذا شرطية وقوله تعالى فيقول جوابها

BAGHAWI:89:15/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:15/r1.claim: A person is tested through blessing; God honors him with wealth and expands his provision, so he concludes that God has honored him by what He gave.
BAGHAWI:89:15/r1.anchor: امتحنه ،   { ربه } بالنعمة ،   { فأكرمه } بالمال ،   { ونعمه } بما وسع عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r1.claim: The person calls wealth an honor and poverty a humiliation; qaddara is read with geminated dāl by Abu Jaʿfar and Ibn Amir, ungeminated by others, and both forms mean to restrict provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر "فقدر" بتشديد الدال، وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say this disbelieving complaint was revealed about Umayya b. Khalaf, who equated wealth with honor and poverty with disgrace.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r3.anchor: وهذا يعني به الكافر، تكون الكرامة والهوان عنده بكثرة المال والحظ في الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r4.claim: God rejects the equation: wealth and poverty are his allotment, not measures of honor; he may enrich an unbeliever or restrict a believer, honoring through obedience and disgracing through sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r4.anchor: فأخبر أن الإكرام والإهانة لا تدور على المال وسعة الرزق، ولكن الفقر والغنى بتقديره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r5.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة وابن كثير ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r5.claim: Hijazi and Basran readers retain the final yāʾ of akramani and ahanani in connected recitation; Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub retain it also at a pause, while others omit it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421/r5.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة "أكرمني وأهانني" بإثبات الياء في الوصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r1.claim: These verses connect to the Lord's watch over the afterlife: people attend only to worldly pleasures although God tests them through both wealth and restricted provision.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r1.anchor: متصل بقوله: { إن ربك لبالمرصاد } كأنه قيل إنه { لبالمرصاد } من الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r2.claim: The person mistakes wealth, status, and ease for proof that God has honored him; the syntax makes the statement the predicate after an intervening conditional circumstance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-16/r2.anchor: اختبره بالغنى واليسر. { فأكرمه ونعمه } بالجاه والمال. { فيقول ربى أكرمن } فضلني بما أعطاني، وهو خبر المبتدأ

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r1.claim: كلا rebukes the person's inference: expansion is generosity, and withholding it is not humiliation; some readers omit the final yāʾ of أكرمن and أهانن, and Ibn ʿĀmir reads قدر with doubled dāl.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r1.anchor: لأن التوسعة تفضل والإخلال به لا يكون إهانة، وقرأ ابن عامر والكوفيون

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r1.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the human addressed as ʿUtba b. Abī Rabīʿa and Abū Ḥudhayfa b. al-Mughīra.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r1.anchor: عتبة بن أبي ربيعة وأبو حذيفة بن المغيرة في رواية عن "ابن عباس"

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil are cited for identifying the person as Ubayy b. Khalaf.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r2.anchor: أو أبي بن خلف فيما روع عن "الكلبي ومقاتل".

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r3.claim: Some exegetes say honor and humiliation refer only to a person's status in the afterlife.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r3.anchor: تأوله بعضهم بأن الإكرام والإهانة لا يكونان في الدنيا

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r4.speaker: الإمام الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r4.claim: A closely related view, chosen by al-Ṭabarī and also found in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, says honor comes through obedience and humiliation through disobedience.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r4.anchor: وهذا التأويل هو ما اختاره الإمام الطبري، ومثله في (البحر المحيط)

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r5.claim: Another view says people cannot know whether apparent blessings or hardships are truly good: wealth may draw one from worship while deprivation may lead to ascetic devotion.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r5.anchor: وقيل إن الإنسان لا يدري حقيقة النعم والنقم

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r6.claim: Other explanations say abundance makes death harder, deprivation makes it easier, wealth brings risks such as theft or killing, or poverty offers safety and peace of mind.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r6.anchor: أو أن النعمة تجعل فراق الدنيا صعباً قاسياً

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r7.claim: Another view says God rejects thanking Him only for abundance and complaining about poverty: a person ought to thank the Creator for both conditions.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r7.anchor: وقيل بل أنكر سبحانه أن يكون حمد الإنسان على نعمه تعالى دون فقره

BINTSHATI:v2p151/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r8.claim: The author reads the context as explicitly presenting both abundance and restricted provision as tests, revealing whether people fulfill gratitude and endure hardship.
BINTSHATI:v2p151/r8.anchor: ونحلص من هذه التأويلات إلى تدبر البيان القرآني.

BINTSHATI:v2p152/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r1.claim: The rebuke targets anyone who assumes wealth proves divine honor and poverty proves that God regards one as contemptible; both states are trials of good and evil.
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r1.anchor: وأن يظن المبتلى بالتضييق أن هذا لهوان أمره على ربه تعالى.

BINTSHATI:v2p152/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r2.speaker: ابن القيم
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says worldly expansion does not prove God's love or a person's true honor, nor does restriction prove humiliation; prosperity and hardship both test people.
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r2.anchor: بل يوسع ويقتر ابتلاءً وامتحاناً. فيبتلى بالنعم كما يبتلى بالمصائب

BINTSHATI:v2p152/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r3.claim: Later verses explain that wealth tests generosity versus greed, poverty tests modesty and patience versus despair, and fighting tests resolve and faith; hardship is also a test of human capacity.
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r3.anchor: وبعد سورة الفجر، نزلت آيات محكمات في مثل هذل الإبتلاء

BINTSHATI:v2p152/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r4.claim: In al-Fajr, privilege can lure people into luxury, corruption, conceit, superiority, and violating others' rights, while deprivation can breed attachment to worldly pleasures and a sense of being forsaken by God.
BINTSHATI:v2p152/r4.anchor: والإبتلاء في سورة الفجر، إنما هو بالنعمة من حيث هي ذريعة ترف وفساد في الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r3.claim: After describing earlier peoples, the passage turns to humanity generally and answers disbelievers who took worldly ease as proof of greater favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r3.anchor: ذكر عادة الإنسان من حيث هو من غير تقييد بهؤلاء الفرق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r4.claim: A test of prosperity may grant social honor, wealth, and ease, which people mistake for deserved divine approval.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r4.anchor: وأعطاه ما يكرمونه به نم الجاه والمال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r5.claim: The prosperous person wrongly treats worldly abundance as proof of personal merit and becomes proud.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p418/r5.anchor: فيظن أن ذلك عن استحقاق فيرتفع به

DURR-FULL:v8p508/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan rejects both inferences: wealth does not prove God honored someone, and poverty does not prove He humiliated them.
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r4.anchor: {فأما الإنسان} الآية قال: كلا اكذبتهما جميعا ما بالغنى أكرمك ولا بالفقر أهانك
