DURR-FULL:v8p508/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r5.claim: Mujāhid says people mistake wealth for divine honor and scarcity for humiliation; honor actually comes through obedience, and humiliation through disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: ظن كرامة الله في المال وهو أنه في قلته وكذب إنما يكرم بطاعته

TAB:89:15/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:15/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:15/r1.claim: When God tests a person with wealth, honors him with money and abundance, the person rejoices and says that his Lord has honored him.
TAB:89:15/r1.anchor: إذا ما امتحنه ربه بالنعم والغنى فَأكْرَمَهُ بالمال ، وأفضل عليه ، وَنَعّمَهُ بما أوسع عليه من فضله

TAB:89:15/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:15/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:15/r2.claim: Qatada comments that the person’s claim that his Lord honored him is true in this instance.
TAB:89:15/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله فَأمّا الإنْسانُ إذَا ما ابْتَلاهُ رَبّهُ فَأكْرَمَهُ وَنَعّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبّي أكْرَمَنِ وحقّ له

BURHAN:v1p400/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p400/r8.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p400/r8.claim: People wrongly infer their standing with God from worldly abundance or constricted provision; God tests both righteous and wicked to establish proof against creation.
BURHAN:v1p400/r8.anchor: هذا الإنسان يعتبر منزلته عند الله في الملكوت بما يبتليه في الدنيا

BURHAN:v2p326/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p326/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p326/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats an appeal for compassion, such as tالله هل قام زيد, as an oath.
BURHAN:v2p326/r2.anchor: ذكر ( 7 ) الزمخشري ان الاستعطاف نحو تالله هل قام زيد قسم

BURHAN:v2p326/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p326/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p326/r3.claim: The author rejects calling an appeal for compassion an oath because it is a declarative statement.
BURHAN:v2p326/r3.anchor: والصحيح انه ليس بقسم لكونه خبرا

BURHAN:v2p326/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p326/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v2p326/r4.claim: Ibn Faris records a distinction in which استخبار is an initial request for information that was not understood, while asking again is استفهام.
BURHAN:v2p326/r4.anchor: حكاه ابن فارس في فقه العربية

BURHAN:v2p326/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p326/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p326/r5.claim: A genuine question requires uncertainty and belief that an answer is possible; otherwise it is redundant or useless.
BURHAN:v2p326/r5.anchor: لزم الا يكون حقيقة الا اذا صدر من شاك مصدق بامكان الاعلام

BURHAN:v2p326/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p326/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p326/r7.claim: When a command follows a question before its answer, it applies to whoever the answer identifies; the example commands honoring whoever is said to have arrived.
BURHAN:v2p326/r7.anchor: الثانية الاستفهام اذا بني عليه امر قبل ذكر الجواب فهم ترتب ذلك الامر على جوابه أي جواب كان

ITQAN:v4p394/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r9.claim: The verses about a person tested by prosperity or restricted provision were revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf.
ITQAN:v4p394/r9.anchor: 5765 ﴿ فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ﴾ الآيات نزلت في أمية بن خلف

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r9.claim: Al-insān in the passage about being tested by one’s Lord refers to Umayya ibn Khalaf.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r9.anchor: العشرون : الإنسان يعني أمية بن خلف . قوله تعالى في سورة الفجر

DAMGHANI:v1p460/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r9.claim: Naʿʿamahu means God expanded a person's livelihood; the source compares God's abundant blessings.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.claim: The first Quranic sense is excellence or superiority, including God’s honoring Adam’s children and the noble book, messenger, and person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكريم في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r1.claim: Exegetes give إن its conditional sense, illustrated by verses that say to act if a stated condition holds.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r1.anchor: وذكر ( 14 / أ ) أهل التفسير أنها في القرآن على أربعة أوجه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r2.claim: Exegetes also use إن in the sense of ما, citing several examples of this construction.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r2.anchor: وذكر ( 14 / أ ) أهل التفسير أنها في القرآن على أربعة أوجه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r3.claim: Exegetes give إن the sense لقد in five cited passages, though Ibn al-Jawzi treats the final example separately as conditional.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r3.anchor: وذكر ( 14 / أ ) أهل التفسير أنها في القرآن على أربعة أوجه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r6.claim: Exegetes list a fourth Quranic sense of إن as إذ, with examples phrased as conditions of belief.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p129/r6.anchor: وذكر ( 14 / أ ) أهل التفسير أنها في القرآن على أربعة أوجه :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.claim: Karīm can mean noble, honored, or excellent: the most God-fearing are best, humanity is honored, and the other examples describe rank or honor.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.anchor: الكريم: الشريف الفاضل، قال الله تعالى: إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم [الحجرات: 13]

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r2.claim: ابتلى is stronger than بلا and more clearly conveys testing; here the test includes being honored and given abundance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r2.anchor: وكلمة ابتلى هي أشد من (بلا) ويظهر فيها معنى الاختبار أكثر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r3.claim: A bala need not be harmful: the verse itself presents testing through honor and favor as well as hardship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p891/r3.anchor: والبلاء قد لا يكون بالضرورة سيئاً والابتلاء اختبار كما في قوله تعالى في سورة الفجر

NASHR:v2p399#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r12.claim: The two Medinan readers, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr retain the final yāʾ in ربي أكرمني and ربي أهانني.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r12.anchor: ربي أكرمني، ربي أهانني فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p191/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p191/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p191/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Jaʿfar retain the final yāʾ in connected recitation of أكرمن and أهانن; al-Bazzī retains it both connected and at pause.
NASHR:v2p191/r1.anchor: فوافقه على إثبات الياء فيهما وصلا نافع وأبو جعفر، وفي الحالين البزي

NASHR:v2p191/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p191/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p191/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr has both forms, with choice more common and deletion the more famous; al-Dānī and al-Shāṭibī choose deletion, which the author calls the better-known report.
NASHR:v2p191/r2.anchor: والوجهان مشهوران عن أبي عمرو والتخيير أكثر والحذف أشهر

NASHR:v2p191/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p191/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p191/r3.claim: Ibn Shanabūdh transmits retention of both yāʾs in both connected recitation and pause from Qunbul.
NASHR:v2p191/r3.anchor: وفي الجامع لابن فارس إثباتهما في الحالين لابن شنبوذ عن قنبل

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r1.claim: The passage reports Quraysh’s claim that wealth and children show divine honor while poverty signals humiliation; they are censured for this widespread assumption.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r1.anchor: ذكر تعالى ما كانت قريش تقوله وتستدل به على إكرام الله تعالى وإهانته لعبده ، فيرون المكرم من عنده الثروة والأولاد ، والمهان ضده .

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r2.claim: Al-insān is a generic term, and this mistaken attitude also appears among many Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r2.anchor: والإنسان اسم جنس ، ويوجد هذا في كثير من أهل الإسلام .

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī connects the passage to the Lord lying in wait: God seeks obedience and final reward, while humans seek immediate pleasure; the author objects to its Muʿtazilī claim that God wills only obedience.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : بم اتصل قوله : { فأما الإنسان } ؟ قلت : بقوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r4.claim: The author says al-Zamakhsharī’s claim that God wills only obedience explicitly reflects Muʿtazilī doctrine.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r4.anchor: وفيه التصريح بمذهب الاعتزال في قوله : لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة .

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r5.claim: The first idhā is governed by yaqūlu, with the sense of speaking at the time of being tested; the fāʾ does not prevent the later verb from governing earlier material.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r5.anchor: وإذا العامل فيه فيقول : والنية فيه التأخير ، أي فيقول كذا وقت الابتداء ، وهذه الفاء لا تمنع أن يعمل ما بعدها فيما قبلها

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r6.claim: After the second ammā an omitted subject balances the first clause; yaqūlu is its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r6.anchor: وبعد أما الثانية مضمر به وقع التوازن بين الجملتين تقديره : فأما إذا هو ما ابتلاه ، وفيقول خبر عن ذلك المبتدأ المضمر

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r7.claim: God tests whether a person is grateful or ungrateful when provision expands, and patient or resentful when it contracts.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r7.anchor: وابتلاه معناه : اختبره ، أيشكر أم يكفر إذا بسط له ؟ وأيصبر أم يجزع إذا ضيق عليه ؟

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r8.claim: The wording pairs granted comfort with constricted provision, not “honored” with “humiliated,” because restricted provision does not itself humiliate; many righteous people, including Dāwūd al-Iṣfahānī, were poor.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r8.anchor: وقابل ونعمه بقوله : { فقدر عليه رزقه } ، ولم يقابل { فأكرمه } بلفظ فأهانه

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r9.claim: The author notes that many righteous people, including Abū Sulaymān Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī al-Iṣfahānī, had restricted provision without being dishonored.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r9.anchor: ألا ترى إلى ناس كثير من أهل الصلاح مضيقاً عليهم الرزق كحال الإمام أبي سليمان داود بن علي الأصبهاني رضي الله تعالى عنه وغيره

ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r10.claim: God censures the claim “my Lord honored me” because the speaker asserts that he deserves and merits this honor.
ABUHAYYAN:89:15/r10.anchor: أما في قوله : { فيقول ربي أكرمن } ، فلأنه إخبار منه على أنه يستحق الكرامة ويستوجبها

ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وباقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains yāʾ in both forms; Nāfiʿ retains it in connected recitation but drops it at pause; Abū ʿAmr permits either; the other seven readers drop it in both positions.
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير : أكرمني وأهانني بالياء فيهما ؛ ونافع : بالياء وصلاً وحذفها وقفاً ، وخير في الوجهين أبو عمرو ، وحذفها باقي السبعة فيهما وصلاً ووقفاً

ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r3.claim: When the yāʾ is dropped at pause, the nūn is given sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN:89:16/r3.anchor: ومن حذفها وقفاً سكن النون فيه .

ALUSI:89:15/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r1.claim: The passage follows the warning that God watches for the afterlife: He seeks striving for it, while people care only for worldly pleasures, rejoicing when they gain and resenting loss.
ALUSI:89:15/r1.anchor: إنه سبحانه لبالمرصاد من أجل الآخرة فلا يطلب عز وجل إلا السعي لها

ALUSI:89:15/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:89:15/r2.claim: Another connection says humans must be punished because wealth leads to pride while poverty makes them impatient, despairing, and prone to improper speech; al-Ālūsī dismisses this account.
ALUSI:89:15/r2.anchor: وقيل هو متصل به متفرع عليه على معنى فالإنسان يؤاخذ لا محالة لأنه بين غني مهلك

ALUSI:89:15/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r3.claim: God treats the person as one tested through wealth and ease, to see whether he gives thanks.
ALUSI:89:15/r3.anchor: عامله معاملة من يبتليه بالغنى واليسار ليرى هل يشكر أم لا

ALUSI:89:15/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r4.claim: The faʾ is explanatory: honoring and granting comfort are precisely what the test means here.
ALUSI:89:15/r4.anchor: تفسيرية فإن الإكرام والتنعيم عين المراد بالابتلاء

ALUSI:89:15/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r5.claim: Because honoring and granting ease amount to one thing, the person's claim says only that God honored him, without adding that He gave him comfort.
ALUSI:89:15/r5.anchor: ولما كان الإكرام والتنعيم في حكم شيء واحد اقتصر على قوله أكرمن

ALUSI:89:15/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r6.claim: The saying clause is the predicate of al-insān; faʾ follows the conditional force of ammā, and the ẓarf idhā belongs to yaqūlu though its position is understood as delayed.
ALUSI:89:15/r6.anchor: خبر للمبتدأ الذي هو الإنسان والفاء لما في أما من معنى الشرط والظرف

ALUSI:89:15/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r7.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو حيان والسمين والسفاقسي
ALUSI:89:15/r7.claim: Zamakhsharī and many later grammarians and exegetes allow the post-faʾ ẓarf to be fronted in its intended attachment to yaqūlu; al-Shihāb calls this the correct analysis.
ALUSI:89:15/r7.anchor: كما صرح به الزمخشري وغيره من متقدمي النحاة وتبعهم من بعدهم كأبي حيان والسمين والسفاقسي

ALUSI:89:15/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r8.speaker: الرضي ومن تبعه
ALUSI:89:15/r8.claim: Al-Raḍī and followers permit fronting after faʾ only when the moved element itself separates ammā from the answer; they disallow another separator and argue deleting the protasis makes faʾ's entry awkward.
ALUSI:89:15/r8.anchor: وخالفهم في ذلك الرضي ومن تبعه كالبدر الدماميني في شرح المغني فقالوا إنما يجوز تقديم ما بعد الفاء

ALUSI:89:15/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r9.speaker: الجلبي
ALUSI:89:15/r9.claim: Al-Jalabī claims consensus against the preceding parse and says the ẓarf belongs to an implicit true subject, شأن الإنسان, so it remains within the separated constituent.
ALUSI:89:15/r9.anchor: وزعم الجلبي محشي المطول أن هذا متفق عليه فرد به على المفسرين

ALUSI:89:15/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:15/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects al-Jalabī's subject تقدير because making the saying clause predicate of شأن requires strained interpretation.
ALUSI:89:15/r10.anchor: ويرد على تقديره أنه لا يصح وقوع جملة يقول خبرا عن الشأن إلا بتعسف

ALUSI:89:15/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:15/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI:89:15/r11.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ treats idhā as conditional, yaqūlu as its answer, and the conditional clause as the predicate of al-insān; this entails omitting faʾ before the saying clause, reportedly by necessity.
ALUSI:89:15/r11.anchor: وذهب أبو البقاء إلى أن إذا شرطية وقوله تعالى فيقول جوابها

BAGHAWI:89:17/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r1.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
BAGHAWI:89:17/r1.claim: The Hijaz and Basra readers retain the yāʾ in the connected forms أكرمني and أهانني.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة أكرمني وأهانني بإثبات الياء في الوصل

BAGHAWI:89:17/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
BAGHAWI:89:17/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub also retain the yāʾ when pausing.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r2.anchor: ويقف ابن كثير ويعقوب بالياء أيضاً

BAGHAWI:89:17/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r3.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI:89:17/r3.claim: The other readers omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused forms.

BAGHAWI:89:17/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:17/r4.claim: Wealth and poverty do not determine honor or humiliation: God grants and restricts provision by decree, including to disbelievers and believers respectively; true honor comes through obedience and disgrace through disobedience.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r4.anchor: فأخبر أن الإكرام والإهانة لا تدور على المال وسعة الرزق ،   ولكن الفقر والغنى بتقديره

BAYDAWI:89:15/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:15/r1.claim: The passage connects to God's watchful attention in 89:14: God attends to the afterlife, while people attend only to worldly pleasure.
BAYDAWI:89:15/r1.anchor: متصل بقوله إن ربك لبالمرصاد كأنه قيل إنه لبالمرصاد من الآخرة

BAYDAWI:89:15/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:15/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:15/r2.claim: The trial here is by wealth and ease; giving status and money leads the person to claim that God has honored him.
BAYDAWI:89:15/r2.anchor: اختبره بالغنى واليسر فأكرمه ونعمه بالجاه والمال

BAYDAWI:89:15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:15/r3.claim: The statement about being honored is the predicate of al-insān; the fāʾ follows the conditional force of ammā, and the time phrase is interpreted as delayed.
BAYDAWI:89:15/r3.anchor: وهو خبر المبتدأ الذي هو الإنسان والفاء لما في أما من معنى الشرط

BIQAI:89:15/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r1.claim: After recounting earlier peoples' tyranny and God's punishment, the passage turns from those groups to humanity generally and answers disbelievers who take worldly prosperity as proof they outrank Muslims.
BIQAI:89:15/r1.anchor: عادة الإنسان من حيث هو من غير تقييد بهؤلاء الفرق عن الابتلاء في حالي السراء والضراء

BIQAI:89:15/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r2.claim: The human was given intellect to understand these divisions and what they require, yet is disposed to forgetfulness, self-love, and self-approval.
BIQAI:89:15/r2.anchor: الذي أودع الحجر ليعقل هذه الأقسام وما يراد منه من اعتقاد المقسم عليه بها وجبل على النسيان

BIQAI:89:15/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r3.claim: The conditional adverb is placed before its predicate to emphasize that the discussion concerns the human's condition at the outset of each trial.
BIQAI:89:15/r3.anchor: قدم الظرف الدال على ذلك على الخبر

BIQAI:89:15/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r4.claim: God tests the person by mixing him with whatever He wills, changing his condition to reveal gratitude or ingratitude; He is the Lord who originated and graciously sustains him.
BIQAI:89:15/r4.anchor: بأن خالطه بما أراد مخالطة تميله وتحيله

BIQAI:89:15/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r5.claim: Being honored means receiving status and wealth that bring respect among people; being favored means comfortable enjoyment without labor for what was given.
BIQAI:89:15/r5.anchor: بأن جعله عزيزاً بين الناس وأعطاه ما يكرمونه به من الجاه والمال

BIQAI:89:15/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:15/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:15/r6.claim: The person says this joyfully and boastfully, wrongly supposing prosperity is deserved, and becomes arrogant because of it.
BIQAI:89:15/r6.anchor: فيظن أن ذلك عن استحقاق فيرتفع به

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: A final yāʾ absent in connected speech can be omitted at pause; retaining it is more analogical and common, since it takes no tanwīn and resembles the yāʾ of قاضي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: وتركها في الوقف أقيس وأكثر لأنها في هذه الحال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: أبو عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ربي أكرمن and ربي أهانن with the possessive yāʾ omitted in pause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو عمرو @QB@ فيقول ربي أكرمن @QE@

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: النابغة
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Al-Nābigha omits final yāʾ in مني and إني; Sībawayh reports this usage from trusted transmitters of Arab speech.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: وقال النابغة # % إذا حاولت في أسد فجورا % فإني لست منك ولست من % يريد مني

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Al-Aʿshā gives further pause forms with a missing possessive yāʾ, including أن يأتين and أنكرن.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Yāʾ in هذا قاضي، هذان غلاماي and رأيت غلامي is not deleted because its preceding consonant is still and its yāʾ is vowelled, unlike pause yāʾ in هذا القاضي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: كياء القاضي في النصب فهي لا تشبه ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Yāʾ is retained in connected يا غلام أقبل because the preceding consonant is still and cannot signal the genitive relation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: ولا تحذف في النداء إذا وصلت كما قلت يا غلام أقبل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: A speaker saying هذا غلامي and إني ذاهب keeps yāʾ at pause because it resembles the vowelled accusative yāʾ; hāʾ may indicate the vowel, while connected vocative allows deletion.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: ومن قال هذا غلامي فاعلم وإني ذاهب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Final alif normally remains at pause even when dropped in connected speech because fatḥa and alif are lighter and Arabic favors alif after an open vowel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: وأما الألفات التي تذهب في الوصل فإنها لا تحذف في الوقف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Some medial vowels are reduced in فخذ and عضد but not جمل because fatḥa is lighter; final alif is otherwise dropped at pause only under poetic necessity.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: ويقولون في فخذ فخذ وفي عضد عضد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.claim: Labīd's verse shortens المعلى to المعل under poetic necessity, showing final alif can be dropped at pause when meter requires.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحذفمنالأسماءمنالياءات.anchor: إلا أن يضطر شاعر فيشبهها بالياء لأنها أختها

DURR:89:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:15/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:15/r1.claim: Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated them; the following verse instead identifies their real disgrace as failing to honor orphans.
DURR:89:15/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : { فأما الإِنسان } الآية

DURR:89:15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:15/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:89:15/r2.claim: Mujahid says people wrongly infer honor from wealth and humiliation from scarcity; God honors through obedience and humiliates through disobedience.
DURR:89:15/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال : ظن كرامة الله في المال وهو أنه في قلته وكذب إنما يكرم بطاعته

DURR:89:16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:16/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:16/r1.claim: Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated them; the following verse instead identifies their real disgrace as failing to honor orphans.
DURR:89:16/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : { فأما الإِنسان } الآية

DURR:89:16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:16/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:89:16/r2.claim: Mujahid says people wrongly infer honor from wealth and humiliation from scarcity; God honors through obedience and humiliates through disobedience.
DURR:89:16/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال : ظن كرامة الله في المال وهو أنه في قلته وكذب إنما يكرم بطاعته

IBNASHUR:89:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r1.claim: The opening fa makes this discussion connected to and derived from what precedes it.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r1.anchor: دلت الفاء على أن الكلام الواقع بعدها متصل بما قبلها ومتفرع عليه لا محالة .

IBNASHUR:89:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r2.claim: Amma means whatever may happen; it strengthens the answer’s connection to the preceding discourse and introduces a contrast.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r2.anchor: ودلت ( أمّا ) على معنى : مهما يكن من شيء

IBNASHUR:89:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r3.claim: After recalling earlier nations’ blessings, heedlessness, and punishment, the passage warns the Quraysh that their luxury and arrogance repeat that pattern.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r3.anchor: اشتمل على وصف ما كانت تتمتع به الأمم الممثّل بها مما أنعم الله عليها به من النعم

IBNASHUR:89:15/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r4.claim: The polytheists mistake prosperity for divine favor, reject the Messenger’s warning as inconsistent with their fortunes, and deny a contrasting afterlife.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r4.anchor: فحسبوا أن إنذار الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم إياهم بالعذاب ليس بصدق لأنه يخالف ما هو واقع لهم من النعمة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r5.claim: Their error rests on denying afterlife and resurrection and imagining worldly conditions endure; they confine reward to wealth and punishment to poverty.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r5.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا الوهَم أصولاً انبنى عليها

IBNASHUR:89:15/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r6.claim: The prefixed fa derives this discussion from the general conclusion that God watches over all, explaining that His course follows knowledge and wisdom.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r6.anchor: فاء التفريع مرتبطة بجملة : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

IBNASHUR:89:15/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r7.claim: The disbeliever supposes that abundance means God honored him, while restricted living means God humiliated him.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r7.anchor: فيتوهم خلاف ذلك إذ يحسب أن ما يناله من نعمة وسعة في الدنيا تكريما من الله له

IBNASHUR:89:15/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r8.claim: Treating prosperity as proof of divine favor implies that God’s actions lack wisdom, a false inference also challenged by the cited verse.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r8.anchor: وهذا التوهم يستلزم ظنهم أفعال الله تعالى جارية على غير حكمة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r9.claim: The warning teaches believers not to let desire distort subtle evidence: worldly states vary and vanish, so they cannot establish a person’s standing with God.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r9.anchor: الأحوال الدنيوية أعراض زائلة ومتفاوتة الطول والقصر

IBNASHUR:89:15/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r10.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR:89:15/r10.claim: Al-Nābigha says the Christian Ghassānids expected consequences and did not imagine that good could come without later evil or evil without lasting consequence.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r10.anchor: قال النابغة في آل غسان الذين لم يكونوا مشركين وكانوا متدينين بالنصرانية

IBNASHUR:89:15/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r11.claim: Poverty is named opposite blessing because the Meccan polytheists generally had healthy, strong bodies and died through killing or old age.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r11.anchor: لأن غالب أحوال المشركين المتحدث عنهم صحة المزاج وقوة الأبدان

IBNASHUR:89:15/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r12.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR:89:15/r12.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line about deadly places not sparing old age illustrates the stated pattern of death.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r12.anchor: قال النابغة : تَغْشَى مَتَالِفَ لا يُنْظِرْنَكَ الهَرَمَا

IBNASHUR:89:15/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r13.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says most commentators did not explain the verse’s arrangement and connection to its context, with al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya as exceptions.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r13.anchor: ولم يعرج أكثر المفسرين على بيان نظم الآية واتصالها بما قبلها عدا الزمخشري وابن عطية

IBNASHUR:89:15/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r14.speaker: طرفة
IBNASHUR:89:15/r14.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse presents wealth and noble sons as a fortunate status that the speaker attributes to his Lord’s choice.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r14.anchor: قال طرفة : فلو شاءَ ربّي كنتُ قيسَ بنَ عاصم

IBNASHUR:89:15/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r15.claim: Quraysh, Tamīm, and Fazāra leaders asked Muhammad to dismiss poor believers, including ʿAmmār, Bilāl, Khabbāb, and Ṣuhayb, promising they might then follow; they made a similar request to Abū Ṭālib.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r15.anchor: لما أتى الملأ من قريش ومن بني تميم وفزارة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r16.claim: Worldly circumstances are no basis for judging recompense for deeds; the consistent recompense comes on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r16.anchor: وأعلمهم أن أحوال الدنيا لا تتخذ أصلا في اعتبار الجزاء على العمل

IBNASHUR:89:15/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r17.claim: Al-insān is a generic expression conventionally encompassing people, but intended here for polytheists who predominate in the audience.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r17.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس وتعريفه تعريف الجنس فيستغرق أفراد الجنس

IBNASHUR:89:15/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r18.claim: This generic usage for disbelievers resembles other Meccan passages and is reinforced by the later reference to the human remembering on that Day.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r18.anchor: { يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان وأنى له الذكرى }

IBNASHUR:89:15/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:89:15/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for identifying the human as either ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa or Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r19.anchor: عتبة بن ربيعة أو أبو حذيفة بن الغيرة عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR:89:15/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r20.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
IBNASHUR:89:15/r20.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī identify the human as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r20.anchor: وقيل : أمية بن خَلَف عن مقاتل والكلبي

IBNASHUR:89:15/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r21.speaker: الكلبي
IBNASHUR:89:15/r21.claim: Al-Kalbī also identifies the human as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r21.anchor: وقيل : أبيّ بن خلف عن الكلبي أيضاً

IBNASHUR:89:15/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r22.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:89:15/r22.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the generic rebuke addresses a tendency prevalent among disbelievers, although some believers may also fall into it.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r22.anchor: قال ابن عطية : ومن حيث كان هذا غالبا على الكفار

IBNASHUR:89:15/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r23.claim: People mistake incidental benefits for God’s honor and harms for targeted vengeance, projecting desire and omens onto events without evidence.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r23.anchor: من ضلال أهل الشرك ومن فتنة الشيطان لبعض جهلة المؤمنين

IBNASHUR:89:15/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r24.claim: Those who call prosperity divine honor are not thereby worthy of God’s honor; those with restricted provision are not lower before Him than the prosperous.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r24.anchor: فهؤلاء الذين زعموا ما نالهم من نعمة الله إكراما من الله لهم ليسوا أهلا لكرامة الله

IBNASHUR:89:15/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r25.claim: This error entrenches polytheism and diverts people from evidence; Ibn al-Rāwandī’s couplet depicts perplexity at the ignorant prospering while the learned suffer.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r25.anchor: عن تزلزل فهمهم وقلة علمهم بقوله

IBNASHUR:89:15/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r26.claim: God’s knowledge is vast and His varied actions follow wisdom; benefits and harms can arrive through several causes, familiar or extraordinary.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r26.anchor: وعلم الله واسع وتصرفاته شتى وكلها صادرة عن حكمة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r27.claim: Worldly openings may precede sudden punishment when people forget admonition and rejoice in what they receive.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r27.anchor: فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r28.claim: After a warning, hardship may be replaced by ease; people wrongly regard both states as ordinary inherited fortune before sudden seizure.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r28.anchor: ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا وقالوا قد مس آباءنا الضراء والسراء

IBNASHUR:89:15/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r29.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r29.claim: People can be tested repeatedly without repenting or remembering, so repeated events should not be read through wishful assumptions.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r29.anchor: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين

IBNASHUR:89:15/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r30.claim: Some divine acts disclose what is intended for people, while others follow the ordained order of the world; the discerning take precautions and defer unclear matters to God.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r30.anchor: بعضها يدل على مراده من الناس وبعضها جار على ما قدره من نظام العالم

IBNASHUR:89:15/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r31.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r31.claim: Guided Muslims should avoid old pagan superstition, though heedless commoners may retain traces of it and should learn from this warning.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r31.anchor: وقد نجد في بعض العوامّ ومن يشبههم من الغافلين بقايا

IBNASHUR:89:15/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r32.claim: God may hasten a good life as reward for a believing person who acts righteously.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r32.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياة طيبة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r33.claim: God may hasten punishment for those who incur His anger; Noah promised his people rain, wealth, and children if they sought forgiveness.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r33.anchor: فقلت استغفروا ربكم إنه كان غفارا يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا ويمددكم بأموال وبنين

IBNASHUR:89:15/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r34.claim: God also promises abundant water if people remain upright on the path.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r34.anchor: وألو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا

IBNASHUR:89:15/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r35.claim: A prominent sign of special divine treatment is that it occurs against the usual pattern, as in the Prophet’s and caliphs’ victories over mighty nations.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r35.anchor: أظهرها أن تجري على خلاف المألوف كما نرى في نصر النبي

IBNASHUR:89:15/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r36.claim: Amma usually introduces a paired contrast, not an unpacking of a prior summary; here it separates ease and abundance from hardship and restricted provision.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r36.anchor: فالمفصل هنا أحوال الإنسان الجاهل فصلت إلى حاله في الخفض والدعة وحاله في الضنك والشدة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r37.claim: The author discussed amma’s use earlier in the commentary on al-Baqara 2:26.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r37.anchor: وقد تقدم ذكر ( أمّا ) عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR:89:15/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r38.claim: Ibtalā means to test; both good and evil test steadfastness, forbearance, patience, and gratitude.

IBNASHUR:89:15/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r39.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r39.claim: The test can measure whether a person gives thanks or is ungrateful, as the cited verse says.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r39.anchor: قال تعالى : { ليبلوني أأشكر أم أكفر }

IBNASHUR:89:15/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r40.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r40.claim: God makes either blessing or restricted provision a test of gratitude, disbelief, patience, or impatience, but the person mistakes it for honor or humiliation.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r40.anchor: إذا جعل ربه ما يناله من النعمة أو من التقتير مظهرا لحاله في الشكر والكفر

IBNASHUR:89:15/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r41.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR:89:15/r41.claim: Al-Rāghib says ikrām may mean conveying an unblemished benefit or making someone or something noble in its kind.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r41.anchor: قال الراغب : أن يُوصَل إلى الإِنسان كرامة

IBNASHUR:89:15/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r42.claim: On al-Rāghib’s distinction, God’s doing ikrām means granting benefit, while the person’s claim means being made noble or eminent.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r42.anchor: وقوله : { فأكرمه } من المعنى الأول للإِكرام

IBNASHUR:89:15/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r43.speaker: المحققون من المتكلمين
IBNASHUR:89:15/r43.claim: The informed theologians, including al-Māturīdī and al-Bāqillānī, hold that unbelievers receive worldly blessings; the Ashʿarī–Māturīdī dispute is verbal.
IBNASHUR:89:15/r43.anchor: والذي عليه المحققون من المتكلمين أن الكافر مُنعَم عليه في الدنيا

IBNASHUR:89:15/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:15/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:15/r44.claim: Naʿʿamahu means that God placed the person in blessing and comfortable living.

IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.claim: There is no contradiction between God granting actual benefits and kallā, because kallā rejects the claim that those benefits prove divine approval.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.anchor: لأن الإبطال وارد على ما قصده

IBNASHUR:89:16/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r22.speaker: نافع
IBNASHUR:89:16/r22.claim: Nāfiʿ retains the yāʾ after each nūn in connected reading but drops it at pause.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r22.anchor: وقرأ نافع : { أكرمن } ، و{ أهانن } بياء بعد النون في الوصل وبحذفها في الوقف

IBNASHUR:89:16/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r23.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR:89:16/r23.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the yāʾ in both connected reading and pause.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r23.anchor: وقرأهما ابن كثير بالياء في الوصل والوقف

IBNASHUR:89:16/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r24.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
IBNASHUR:89:16/r24.claim: These readers omit the yāʾ in both connected reading and pause; the consonantal rasm lacks the yāʾ, without conflicting with transmitted readings.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r24.anchor: وقرأهما ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب بدون ياء في الوصل والوقف

IBNATIYYA:89:15/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r1.claim: Quraysh treated wealth, prosperity, and children as proof God honored someone, and their absence as proof of humiliation; the rebuke addresses humanity because this tendency also occurs among some believers.
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r1.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى في هذه الآية : ما كانت قريش تقوله

IBNATIYYA:89:15/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r2.claim: The generic singular “the human” broadens the rebuke beyond the disbelievers, since some believers also fall into this way of thinking.
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r2.anchor: ومن حيث كان هذا المقطع غالباً على كثيرين من الكفار ، جاء التوبيخ في هذه الآية لاسم الجنس ، إذ يقع بعض المؤمنين في شيء من هذا المنزع

IBNATIYYA:89:15/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r3.speaker: الأعراب
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r3.claim: The Bedouins who came to Medina called the religion good when they received good fortune and bad when misfortune struck them.
IBNATIYYA:89:15/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك حديث الأعراب الذين كانوا يقدمون المدينة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فمن نال خيراً قال هذا دين حسن ، ومن ناله شر قال هذا دين سوء

IBNATIYYA:89:16/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the final yāʾ in akramanī in both connection and pause; Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i omit it in both.
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «أكرمني » بالياء في وصل ووقف وحذفها عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي في الوجهين :

IBNATIYYA:89:16/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r3.claim: Nafi keeps the yāʾ in connected recitation but drops it at a pause, likewise for ahānanī; Abu Amr permits either form in both cases.
IBNATIYYA:89:16/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع بالياء في الوصل وحذفها في الوقف ، وكذلك «أهانني » ، وخير في الوجهين أبو عمرو

KASHSHAF:89:15/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r1.claim: This passage connects to the Lord keeping watch: God seeks human obedience and preparation for the afterlife and watches for the disobedient with punishment, while people pursue immediate pleasures.
KASHSHAF:89:15/r1.anchor: إن الله لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة والسعي للعاقبة

KASHSHAF:89:15/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r2.claim: The two clauses balance through an implicit subject in the second: the first man's predicate is “he says,” while the intervening time phrase is delayed; the second “he says” likewise needs an understood subject.
KASHSHAF:89:15/r2.anchor: هما متوازنان من حيث إن التقدير

KASHSHAF:89:15/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r3.claim: Both wealth's expansion and its restriction test the servant: abundance tests gratitude rather than ingratitude, and constraint tests patience rather than dismay; their wisdom is the same.
KASHSHAF:89:15/r3.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

KASHSHAF:89:15/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r4.claim: Calling abundance honor is proper because it is a freely bestowed favor; restricted provision is not humiliation, since withholding a favor is not an insult, and a patron may neither honor nor humiliate.

KASHSHAF:89:15/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r5.claim: One answer is that the rebuke targets claiming wealth was deserved because of one's status or ancestry; God grants it freely, and regards piety rather than lineage and pedigree as worthy of honor.
KASHSHAF:89:15/r5.anchor: إنما أنكر قوله ربي أكرمن وذمه عليه

KASHSHAF:89:15/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r6.claim: A second answer carries the rebuke over to “my Lord humiliated me”: people acknowledge God's generosity when favored but wrongly call the absence of a favor humiliation.
KASHSHAF:89:15/r6.anchor: والثاني : أن ينساق الإنكار والذمّ إلى قوله : { رَبّى أَهَانَنِ }

KASHSHAF:89:15/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:15/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:15/r7.claim: Reported readings have qaddara with a light or doubled dāl; at pause, akraman and ahānan have a still nūn for readers who omit the yāʾ in continuation, relying on its kasra.

NASAFI:89:15/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r3.claim: A person should strive for the afterlife and not fret over immediate fortune, but reverses this: he reads abundance as honor and deprivation as humiliation, caring only for present pleasures.
NASAFI:89:15/r3.anchor: الواجب لمن ربه بالمرصاد أن يسعى للعاقبة ولا تهمه العاجلة

NASAFI:89:15/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r4.claim: When tested by blessing and plenty, the person should be grateful; instead he claims God honored and preferred him by granting wealth, mistaking worldly abundance for honor.
NASAFI:89:15/r4.anchor: فإنه إذا امتحنه ربه بالنعمة والسعة ليشكر ، قال : ربي أكرمني أي فضلني بما أعطاني

NASAFI:89:15/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r6.claim: Kalla rejects the claim that honor and humiliation are measured by wealth: honor comes from enabling obedience, and humiliation from being forsaken.
NASAFI:89:15/r6.anchor: ليس الإكرام والإهانة في كثرة المال وقلته بل الإكرام في توفيق الطاعة

NASAFI:89:15/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r7.claim: Each fa-yaqulu is the predicate of its subject; the first follows al-insan, with the intervening time phrase syntactically delayed, and the second predicates an implied subject. The fa follows amma’s conditional sense.
NASAFI:89:15/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فَيَقُولُ } خبر المبتدأ الذي هو الإنسان ، ودخول الفاء لما في «أما » من معنى الشرط

NASAFI:89:15/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r8.claim: Both expanded and restricted provision are tests: abundance tests whether one gives thanks or is ungrateful, while restriction tests whether one is patient or distressed.
NASAFI:89:15/r8.anchor: وسمى كلا الأمرين من بسط الرزق وتقديره ابتلاء لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

NASAFI:89:15/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:15/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:15/r9.claim: God rejects the person’s claim that wealth proves deserved honor, though He does say He bestowed and enriched him: the gift was a test, not earned; Nasafi compares the error to Qarun’s claim that his wealth came through his own knowledge.
NASAFI:89:15/r9.anchor: وإنما أنكر قوله { رَبّى أَكْرَمَنِ } مع أنه أثبته بقوله { فَأَكْرَمَهُ } لأنه قاله على قصد خلاف

NASAFI:89:16/r3.speaker: author

NASAFI:89:16/r8.anchor: وسمى كلا الأمرين من بسط الرزق وتقديره ابتلاء لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

NASAFI:89:20/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r3.speaker: الحجازي وأبو عمرو
NASAFI:89:20/r3.claim: The Hijazis and Abu ‘Amr have the cited reading of rabbi in the preceding verses.

QURTUBI:89:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:15/r1.claim: The human being in this passage means the unbeliever.
QURTUBI:89:15/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " فأما الإنسان " يعني الكافر

QURTUBI:89:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:89:15/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person as Utba ibn Rabia and Abu Hudhayfa ibn al-Mughira.
QURTUBI:89:15/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا حذيفة بن المغيرة

QURTUBI:89:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:89:15/r3.claim: Another view identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf.

QURTUBI:89:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:89:15/r4.claim: A further view identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

QURTUBI:89:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:15/r5.claim: God tests and tries him through blessing; ما is an added particle.
QURTUBI:89:15/r5.anchor: " إذا ما ابتلاه ربه " أي امتحنه واختبره بالنعمة . و " ما " : زائدة صلة

QURTUBI:89:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:15/r6.claim: God honors him with wealth and grants him comfort by giving him abundance.
QURTUBI:89:15/r6.anchor: " فأكرمه " بالمال . " ونعمه " بما أوسع عليه

QURTUBI:89:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:15/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:15/r7.claim: He boasts that God honored him, rejoicing in his wealth without thanking God.
QURTUBI:89:15/r7.anchor: " فيقول ربي أكرمني " فيفرح بذلك ولا يحمده

RAZI:89:15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r1.claim: The passage connects to God's being in wait at the resurrection: people should strive for the afterlife, but this person cares only for worldly desires.
RAZI:89:15/r1.anchor: قوله : { فأما الإنسان } متعلق بقوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

RAZI:89:15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r2.claim: The person reads worldly comfort as God's honoring him and lack of comfort as God's humiliation of him.
RAZI:89:15/r2.anchor: فإن وجد الراحة في الدنيا يقول : ربي أكرمني

RAZI:89:15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī compares this worldly outlook to people who know only the outward life of this world and neglect the afterlife.
RAZI:89:15/r3.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في صفة الكفار : { يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا

RAZI:89:15/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r4.claim: He also compares it to the person who worships God conditionally, content when blessed but turning away when tested.
RAZI:89:15/r4.anchor: وقال : { ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير

RAZI:89:15/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r5.claim: First, worldly happiness is negligible beside afterlife happiness: worldly comfort ending in afterlife misery is no happiness, and worldly pain ending in salvation is no humiliation.
RAZI:89:15/r5.anchor: أن سعادة الدنيا وشقاوتها في مقابلة ما في الآخرة من السعادة والشقاوة كالقطرة في البحر

RAZI:89:15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r6.claim: A person therefore cannot decide that worldly ease proves final honor or that worldly suffering proves final disgrace.
RAZI:89:15/r6.anchor: إذ المتنعم في الدنيا لا يجوز له أن يحكم على نفسه بالسعادة والكرامة

RAZI:89:15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r7.claim: Second, worldly wealth and pain do not establish merit: God may expand for sinners or unbelievers by His will, for wise purposes, or as a means of entrapment, and may constrict the righteous for corresponding reasons.
RAZI:89:15/r7.anchor: فإنه تعالى كثيرا ما يوسع على العصاة والكفرة

RAZI:89:15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r8.claim: Neither expansion nor constriction should be assumed to be recompense for what a person deserves.
RAZI:89:15/r8.anchor: وقد يضيق على الصديقين لأضداد ما ذكرنا

RAZI:89:15/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r9.claim: Third, those enjoying wealth must consider the final outcome; the poor must remember God's boundless gifts of bodily, intellectual, and religious well-being and protection from countless harms.
RAZI:89:15/r9.anchor: والفقير والمحتاج لا ينبغي أن يغفل عما لله عليه من النعم

RAZI:89:15/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r10.claim: A poor person should not pronounce himself humiliated without qualification.
RAZI:89:15/r10.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن يقضي على نفسه بالإهانة مطلقا

RAZI:89:15/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r11.claim: Fourth, sensual habits and desires make attachment to worldly pleasures hard to break, while deprivation turns a person back to God and worship.
RAZI:89:15/r11.anchor: أما إذا لم يحصل للإنسان شيء من هذه المحسوسات رجعت شاءت أم أبت إلى الله

RAZI:89:15/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r12.claim: Finding the world may deprive one of closeness to God, while lacking it can be a means to the greatest happiness.
RAZI:89:15/r12.anchor: فكان وجدان الدنيا سببا للحرمان من الله

RAZI:89:15/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r13.claim: Fifth, lasting experience intensifies love, and stronger love makes separation more painful; abundant worldly enjoyment can therefore increase pain at death.
RAZI:89:15/r13.anchor: أن كثرة الممارسة سبب لتأكد المحبة

RAZI:89:15/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r14.claim: Conversely, less attachment may mean greater afterlife happiness, so possession is not necessarily happiness and deprivation is not necessarily misery.
RAZI:89:15/r14.anchor: فإذن حصول لذات الدنيا سبب للألم الشديد بعد الموت

RAZI:89:15/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r15.claim: These arguments presuppose belief in bodily or spiritual resurrection; someone denying every form of resurrection would otherwise have to equate possession with happiness and deprivation with misery.
RAZI:89:15/r15.anchor: أن هذه الوجوه إنما تصح مع القول بإثبات البعث روحانيا كان أو جسمانيا

RAZI:89:15/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r16.claim: Even one who denies resurrection cannot confidently judge by wealth alone, since great wealth may bring murder, robbery, and torment while deprivation may preserve safety.
RAZI:89:15/r16.anchor: أنه ربما كان وجدان الدنيا الكثيرة سببا للقتل والنهب والوقوع في أنواع العذاب

RAZI:89:15/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:89:15/r17.claim: One reported view says the human denotes two particular people: ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra.
RAZI:89:15/r17.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس أنه عتبة بن ربيعة

RAZI:89:15/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r18.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:89:15/r18.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
RAZI:89:15/r18.anchor: وقال الكلبي : هو أبي بن خلف

RAZI:89:15/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r19.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:89:15/r19.claim: Muqātil says the passage was revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf.
RAZI:89:15/r19.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

RAZI:89:15/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r20.claim: The other view takes 'the human' as anyone characterized by this description: an unbeliever who denies the Day of Recompense.
RAZI:89:15/r20.anchor: أن المراد من كان موصوفا بهذا الوصف وهو الكافر الجاحد ليوم الجزاء

RAZI:89:15/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r21.claim: Both expansion and restriction are tests: expansion tests gratitude or ingratitude, while restriction tests patience or despair.
RAZI:89:15/r21.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

RAZI:89:15/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r22.claim: Al-Rāzī compares these paired tests with the statement that God tests people with good and evil as a trial.
RAZI:89:15/r22.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة }

RAZI:89:15/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r23.claim: One possible answer to the apparent rebuke is that 'No!' rejects only the claim that God humiliated the person in poverty.
RAZI:89:15/r23.anchor: لأن كلمة الإنكار هي قوله : { كلا }

RAZI:89:15/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r24.claim: If the rebuke covers both claims, one explanation is that the person assumes the wealth was deserved.
RAZI:89:15/r24.anchor: سلمنا أن الإنكار عائد إليهما معا ولكن فيه وجوه ثلاثة

RAZI:89:15/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r25.claim: A second explanation is that God's gifts of bodily health, reason, and religion preceded wealth; acknowledging blessing only upon gaining money shows boasting, not gratitude.
RAZI:89:15/r25.anchor: أن نعم الله تعالى كانت حاصلة قبل وجدان المال

RAZI:89:15/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r26.claim: Boasting of worldly gifts while ignoring afterlife blessings signals denial of resurrection, as in the owner of the garden who doubts the Hour.
RAZI:89:15/r26.anchor: أن تصلفه بنعمة الدنيا وإعراضه عن ذكر نعمة الآخرة

RAZI:89:15/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r27.claim: The first clause uses fāʾ and the second wāw because mercy precedes anger and testing by blessings precedes testing by pain; the more frequent blessing is put first.
RAZI:89:15/r27.anchor: لأن رحمة الله سابقة على غضبه وابتلاءه بالنعم سابق على ابتلائه بإنزال الآلام

RAZI:89:15/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r28.claim: The text says God honored the person but does not say He humiliated him: the first claim is true, while treating reduced provision as humiliation is false.

RAZI:89:15/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:15/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:89:15/r31.claim: At pause, the final nūn of akramani and ahānani is unvocalized for readers who omit the yāʾ in connected speech and rely on its kasra.
RAZI:89:15/r31.anchor: وأكرمن وأهانن بسكون النون في الوقف فيمن ترك الياء في الدرج مكتفيا منها بالكسرة

RAZI:89:16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r1.claim: The passage connects to God's being in wait at the resurrection: people should strive for the afterlife, but this person cares only for worldly desires.
RAZI:89:16/r1.anchor: قوله : { فأما الإنسان } متعلق بقوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

RAZI:89:16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r2.claim: The person reads worldly comfort as God's honoring him and lack of comfort as God's humiliation of him.
RAZI:89:16/r2.anchor: فإن وجد الراحة في الدنيا يقول : ربي أكرمني

RAZI:89:16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī compares this worldly outlook to people who know only the outward life of this world and neglect the afterlife.
RAZI:89:16/r3.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في صفة الكفار : { يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا

RAZI:89:16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r4.claim: He also compares it to the person who worships God conditionally, content when blessed but turning away when tested.
RAZI:89:16/r4.anchor: وقال : { ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير

RAZI:89:16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r5.claim: First, worldly happiness is negligible beside afterlife happiness: worldly comfort ending in afterlife misery is no happiness, and worldly pain ending in salvation is no humiliation.
RAZI:89:16/r5.anchor: أن سعادة الدنيا وشقاوتها في مقابلة ما في الآخرة من السعادة والشقاوة كالقطرة في البحر

RAZI:89:16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r6.claim: A person therefore cannot decide that worldly ease proves final honor or that worldly suffering proves final disgrace.
RAZI:89:16/r6.anchor: إذ المتنعم في الدنيا لا يجوز له أن يحكم على نفسه بالسعادة والكرامة

RAZI:89:16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r7.claim: Second, worldly wealth and pain do not establish merit: God may expand for sinners or unbelievers by His will, for wise purposes, or as a means of entrapment, and may constrict the righteous for corresponding reasons.
RAZI:89:16/r7.anchor: فإنه تعالى كثيرا ما يوسع على العصاة والكفرة

RAZI:89:16/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r8.claim: Neither expansion nor constriction should be assumed to be recompense for what a person deserves.
RAZI:89:16/r8.anchor: وقد يضيق على الصديقين لأضداد ما ذكرنا

RAZI:89:16/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r9.claim: Third, those enjoying wealth must consider the final outcome; the poor must remember God's boundless gifts of bodily, intellectual, and religious well-being and protection from countless harms.
RAZI:89:16/r9.anchor: والفقير والمحتاج لا ينبغي أن يغفل عما لله عليه من النعم

RAZI:89:16/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r10.claim: A poor person should not pronounce himself humiliated without qualification.
RAZI:89:16/r10.anchor: فلا ينبغي أن يقضي على نفسه بالإهانة مطلقا

RAZI:89:16/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r11.claim: Fourth, sensual habits and desires make attachment to worldly pleasures hard to break, while deprivation turns a person back to God and worship.
RAZI:89:16/r11.anchor: أما إذا لم يحصل للإنسان شيء من هذه المحسوسات رجعت شاءت أم أبت إلى الله

RAZI:89:16/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r12.claim: Finding the world may deprive one of closeness to God, while lacking it can be a means to the greatest happiness.
RAZI:89:16/r12.anchor: فكان وجدان الدنيا سببا للحرمان من الله

RAZI:89:16/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r13.claim: Fifth, lasting experience intensifies love, and stronger love makes separation more painful; abundant worldly enjoyment can therefore increase pain at death.
RAZI:89:16/r13.anchor: أن كثرة الممارسة سبب لتأكد المحبة

RAZI:89:16/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r14.claim: Conversely, less attachment may mean greater afterlife happiness, so possession is not necessarily happiness and deprivation is not necessarily misery.
RAZI:89:16/r14.anchor: فإذن حصول لذات الدنيا سبب للألم الشديد بعد الموت

RAZI:89:16/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r15.claim: These arguments presuppose belief in bodily or spiritual resurrection; someone denying every form of resurrection would otherwise have to equate possession with happiness and deprivation with misery.
RAZI:89:16/r15.anchor: أن هذه الوجوه إنما تصح مع القول بإثبات البعث روحانيا كان أو جسمانيا

RAZI:89:16/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r16.claim: Even one who denies resurrection cannot confidently judge by wealth alone, since great wealth may bring murder, robbery, and torment while deprivation may preserve safety.
RAZI:89:16/r16.anchor: أنه ربما كان وجدان الدنيا الكثيرة سببا للقتل والنهب والوقوع في أنواع العذاب

RAZI:89:16/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:89:16/r17.claim: One reported view says the human denotes two particular people: ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and Abū Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Mughīra.
RAZI:89:16/r17.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس أنه عتبة بن ربيعة

RAZI:89:16/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r18.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:89:16/r18.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
RAZI:89:16/r18.anchor: وقال الكلبي : هو أبي بن خلف

RAZI:89:16/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r19.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:89:16/r19.claim: Muqātil says the passage was revealed concerning Umayya ibn Khalaf.
RAZI:89:16/r19.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أمية بن خلف

RAZI:89:16/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r20.claim: The other view takes 'the human' as anyone characterized by this description: an unbeliever who denies the Day of Recompense.
RAZI:89:16/r20.anchor: أن المراد من كان موصوفا بهذا الوصف وهو الكافر الجاحد ليوم الجزاء

RAZI:89:16/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r21.claim: Both expansion and restriction are tests: expansion tests gratitude or ingratitude, while restriction tests patience or despair.
RAZI:89:16/r21.anchor: لأن كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد

RAZI:89:16/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r22.claim: Al-Rāzī compares these paired tests with the statement that God tests people with good and evil as a trial.
RAZI:89:16/r22.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة }

RAZI:89:16/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r23.claim: One possible answer to the apparent rebuke is that 'No!' rejects only the claim that God humiliated the person in poverty.
RAZI:89:16/r23.anchor: لأن كلمة الإنكار هي قوله : { كلا }

RAZI:89:16/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r24.claim: If the rebuke covers both claims, one explanation is that the person assumes the wealth was deserved.
RAZI:89:16/r24.anchor: سلمنا أن الإنكار عائد إليهما معا ولكن فيه وجوه ثلاثة

RAZI:89:16/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r25.claim: A second explanation is that God's gifts of bodily health, reason, and religion preceded wealth; acknowledging blessing only upon gaining money shows boasting, not gratitude.
RAZI:89:16/r25.anchor: أن نعم الله تعالى كانت حاصلة قبل وجدان المال

RAZI:89:16/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r26.claim: Boasting of worldly gifts while ignoring afterlife blessings signals denial of resurrection, as in the owner of the garden who doubts the Hour.
RAZI:89:16/r26.anchor: أن تصلفه بنعمة الدنيا وإعراضه عن ذكر نعمة الآخرة

RAZI:89:16/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r27.claim: The first clause uses fāʾ and the second wāw because mercy precedes anger and testing by blessings precedes testing by pain; the more frequent blessing is put first.
RAZI:89:16/r27.anchor: لأن رحمة الله سابقة على غضبه وابتلاءه بالنعم سابق على ابتلائه بإنزال الآلام

RAZI:89:16/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r28.claim: The text says God honored the person but does not say He humiliated him: the first claim is true, while treating reduced provision as humiliation is false.

RAZI:89:16/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:16/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:89:16/r31.claim: At pause, the final nūn of akramani and ahānani is unvocalized for readers who omit the yāʾ in connected speech and rely on its kasra.
RAZI:89:16/r31.anchor: وأكرمن وأهانن بسكون النون في الوقف فيمن ترك الياء في الدرج مكتفيا منها بالكسرة

RAZI:89:17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:89:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God does not test someone with riches because He honors him or with poverty because He despises him.
RAZI:89:17/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى لم ابتله بالغنى لكرامته علي

RAZI:89:17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r5.claim: God may expand an unbeliever's wealth without honoring him or restrict a believer without despising him.
RAZI:89:17/r5.anchor: فقد يوسع على الكافر لا لكرامته
